guides.title: Overview
guides.description: Product model, chat infrastructure concepts, and integration principles.
guides.text:
Start here

# Add chat to your app with ConvoKit.

Connect your users, open conversations, and send messages using a core SDK or ready-made UI library.

### Your first integration

1.  [Choose your platform](https://convokit.app/docs/sdks) and decide whether to use ready-made UI or build your own.
2.  Follow the [quickstart](https://convokit.app/docs/quickstart) to create an app and add an authenticated token endpoint to your backend.
3.  Use your platform guide to connect a user, open a conversation, and send a message.

Already integrated? Read about [message state and read receipts](https://convokit.app/docs/messaging), browse the [API reference](https://convokit.app/docs/api-reference), or open the [dashboard guide](https://convokit.app/docs/operations).

### Core model

The pieces every chat integration uses, whether it starts with REST or an SDK.

### App

An app contains credentials, users, conversations, messages, and settings for one product surface.

### App user

A product user identity synced into ConvoKit so clients can receive scoped chat access.

### Conversation

A chat between app users, with messages, attachments, and a membership role for each participant.

### Integration principles

Keep credentials safe and connect the correct product user.

**Keep secrets server-side**Store app secrets in backend environments and never ship them in a browser or mobile bundle.

**Map users consistently**Use stable product user IDs within each ConvoKit app. Matching external IDs in different apps remain independent.

**Create the user before issuing a token**Create or sync the app user before issuing a scoped user token for that identity.

**Use scoped client access**Call client-safe routes with user tokens instead of app-level credentials.

guides.title: Authentication
guides.description: Server credentials, scoped user tokens, and trusted client handoff.
guides.text:
Authentication

# ConvoKit separates app credentials from end-user chat sessions.

Your backend keeps the secret, maps product users to app users, and gives clients scoped, expiring access.

### Admin routes

Server-side routes for user sync, token issuance, conversation management, and moderation workflows.

`x-client-id``x-client-secret`

### SDK routes

Client-safe routes for signed-in app users. The bearer token represents one product user in one ConvoKit app.

`x-client-id``authorization: Bearer <token>`

### Authenticate your product user before issuing a chat token.

-   Protect your token endpoint with your existing product authentication.
-   Derive the ConvoKit app user ID from the verified session, not an ID in the request body.
-   If a client requests a different identity, reject it.
-   The public client ID is not authentication.

User IDs are app-scoped: the same external ID in two apps represents independent users. Create or sync the user before issuing a token. Deleting and recreating an ID does not reactivate its old tokens; reconnect with a freshly issued token. Use the token returned by your backend as-is; your client does not create or modify it.

Your token provider must call your backend with product-session credentials and return the scoped token string. Return token responses with Cache-Control: no-store. For cookie-based authentication, enforce your normal CSRF protections; for native clients, attach your product access token. See the [authenticated token example](https://convokit.app/docs/quickstart) and the [dashboard setup guide](https://convokit.app/docs/operations#operations-setup).

### Realtime configuration is managed for you.

-   Configure your public ConvoKit client ID and token provider, then call connectUser.
-   The SDK connects to https://api.convokit.app automatically and manages the realtime connection.
-   No additional service credentials or connection URLs are needed.

READ members can receive messages and submit read receipts. READ\_WRITE members can also send messages, publish typing state, and upload conversation media. Your app secret stays on your backend; it is never client configuration.

Your backend decides who may join a conversation. A room ID alone does not grant access. When membership ends, stop displaying that room in your app. Removing access cannot retract data already received or downloaded; events sent before removal may still arrive.

guides.text:
MCP integration

# Add ConvoKit to your coding assistant.

Connect to our public Developer MCP server for official guides, exact code examples, and a plan tailored to your platform. No account, app ID, or secret is required.

### Connect to the Developer server

Use this URL in any MCP client that supports Streamable HTTP.

```text
https://convokit-mcp.suryadeep.workers.dev/mcp/developer
```

The Developer server reads documentation. It cannot access your users, conversations, messages, or app credentials.

### Codex

Run this command to add the public connection.

```bash
codex mcp add convokit_developer --url https://convokit-mcp.suryadeep.workers.dev/mcp/developer
```

Or add this entry to `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
[mcp_servers.convokit_developer]
url = "https://convokit-mcp.suryadeep.workers.dev/mcp/developer"
```

Restart Codex or refresh its MCP connections, then verify that the ConvoKit tools are available. See the [official Codex MCP setup documentation](https://developers.openai.com/codex/mcp) for configuration options.

### Cursor and other MCP clients

Add this configuration to .cursor/mcp.json. Other clients can use the same endpoint through their remote MCP settings.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "convokit_developer": {
      "url": "https://convokit-mcp.suryadeep.workers.dev/mcp/developer"
    }
  }
}
```

Enable or refresh the connection in your assistant. Client configuration formats vary; use Streamable HTTP with no authorization header. In clients with a remote connector dialog, paste the Developer endpoint directly.

### Ask your assistant to integrate ConvoKit

Start with a platform and the chat experience you want to build.

-   “Use ConvoKit to add support chat to this React app. Plan the integration and adapt the token endpoint to our existing authentication.”
-   “Find the SwiftUI conversation example and add read receipts.”
-   “Set up ConvoKit in this Flutter app using the official SDK and UI library.”

Supported platforms: JavaScript, React, Vue, React Native, Flutter, Swift, and Android. The assistant can inspect your project, fetch the matching examples, and adapt them to your code.

### Developer tools

All five tools read the official ConvoKit guides. Responses include source URLs and a documentation snapshot date.

-   `get_integration_plan`: choose the SDK and UI guides, backend token steps, and connection flow for your platform.
-   `search_docs`: find relevant sections by topic or API name.
-   `list_guides`: discover the available guides, optionally filtered by platform.
-   `get_guide`: read a guide’s section index or a selected section.
-   `get_code_examples`: fetch exact examples from a guide, filter by topic, and paginate results.

Clients that support MCP resources can also read complete guides at `convokit://docs/<guide-id>`. The `integrate_convokit` prompt prepares a task from your platform and goal.

The server uses a bundled documentation snapshot. Follow the returned guide URLs and documented package versions when reviewing an integration. Your assistant still needs access to your project to edit your code.

### Optional: manage an app with a second connection

The App MCP server runs locally with credentials for one ConvoKit app. Use both connections when you want guidance and app management.

Open your app in the [dashboard](https://dashboard.convokit.app/) and choose **MCP integration**. Owners and admins get a configuration with the selected app’s ID. Node.js 22.20 or later is required for the local App server.

The versioned launch command is:

```bash
npx -y github:ConvoKitApp/ConvoKit-MCP#v0.1.0 app
```

Set `CONVOKIT_CLIENT_ID` and `CONVOKIT_CLIENT_SECRET` in the local MCP process’s environment. The dashboard provides Codex and JSON setup examples. Keep secrets in a trusted local environment or private configuration outside source control.

The App server can sync users, issue user tokens, manage conversation membership, and update or delete conversations and messages. It uses app administrator credentials: give it only to trusted assistants and review their proposed changes. Add a separate named App connection for each app you want to manage.

Implementation, local setup, and release details are available in the [ConvoKit MCP repository](https://github.com/ConvoKitApp/ConvoKit-MCP).

guides.description: Sending state, read receipts, timestamps, retries, and automatic UI behavior.
guides.text:
Messaging behavior

# Understand message state without building it twice.

Use SDK-backed UI for built-in chat behavior, or use the core SDK and these rules when your app owns the interface.

### What is automatic?

The core SDK manages the authenticated connection and token renewal through your token provider. SDK-backed UI adds history loading, pagination, sending state, editing and deleting the user’s own messages, typing indicators, and read-receipt state.

SDK-backed conversation lists show message previews, unread counts and the user’s own unread marker, and refresh after conversation changes, message activity, and reconnects. Open conversations catch up after a temporary disconnection. You do not need to recreate the client for a temporary network interruption.

Controlled views display the state and callbacks you supply. They do not fetch messages, refresh an inbox, or submit read receipts on their own. Your app also owns sign-in, room-joining policy, navigation, and file picking.

### Sending, sent, and read are different states

-   **Sending:** the message is pending confirmation. SDK-backed UI shows Sending… without a provisional timestamp or read receipt.
-   **Sent:** ConvoKit has accepted the message. This does not prove delivery to a device or that someone has read it.
-   **Read:** a recipient has reported reading the conversation through that message. A missing receipt does not prove the message was unseen.

In the default UI, pending rows show Sending…, a confirmed message without readers is marked Sent (single check), and read state shows Read by N (double check) on most platforms; see each UI guide for its exact icons. ConvoKit does not currently report recipient delivery.

Confirmed message timestamps display in the viewing device’s timezone in the default UI. A custom renderer should format the message’s `createdAt` in local time, without adding or subtracting a timezone offset manually.

### Read receipts

A read is a position, not a timestamp. When a member reports a read, ConvoKit records the newest message they had actually seen as their read position and decides which messages that read covers by conversation order. A read that reaches the server after a newer message arrived therefore leaves that newer message unread. Positions never move backward; reporting an older message after a newer one changes nothing.

For custom UI, start with each participant’s `readPosition` and `lastReadAt`, and update both from `onReadReceipt` events, which carry `userId`, `readAt`, and `readPosition`. Apply one rule per participant: when they have a read position, they have read every message at or before it (compare `createdAt`, then the message ID); when they only have `lastReadAt`, which is the case for reads recorded before positions existed or in a conversation that had no messages yet, the message is read when that time is at or after its `createdAt`. The core SDKs export `covers` and `readThrough` helpers that apply this rule. Do not count the sender as a recipient.

Call `markConversationRead` with `throughMessageId` set to the newest message the user has actually seen. Omit it only when you cannot name a message; the position then becomes the newest message on the server at request time. Both READ and READ\_WRITE members can report reads. SDK-backed UI offers `markReadOnLoad` and `markReadOnReceive`; configure these to match your app’s visibility rules. It reports the newest rendered message, and only while the conversation is active and visible: a read held back while the screen was hidden is sent once it is visible again. Controlled views need your read handler.

Precise receipts need both sides on 0.5.0 or newer of their SDK and UI packages: the reader’s client to name the message it saw, and the viewer’s client to compare by position. Earlier readers still report reads through the newest message on the server, and earlier viewers still show receipts by comparing `lastReadAt` with `createdAt`.

Read receipts indicate a reported read position, not proof of attention or comprehension.

### Inbox previews and unread counts

An inbox is the list of conversations the user belongs to, ordered by latest activity, with each conversation’s latest message and an unread count. The core SDKs return it from `listInbox`, one page at a time behind an opaque cursor, and SDK-backed conversation lists show it by default. Each entry carries the conversation, its latest message (or null when the conversation has no messages), `unreadCount`, `unreadCountCapped`, the user’s own `readPosition` and `lastReadAt`, and `activityAt`.

Ordering follows the latest surviving message: a conversation sorts by the time of its newest message, never earlier than its own creation time, so an empty conversation sorts by when it was created. Editing a message changes the preview but does not move the conversation. Deleting the latest message recalculates the preview and the position, so the conversation moves down to its next newest message or back to its creation time.

The unread count is the number of messages from other users after the user’s read position; their own messages never count. It is exact up to 1,000. When more than 1,000 messages follow the position, the count is a lower bound over the first 1,000 and `unreadCountCapped` is true; the default UI shows such a count as `99+`. Because own messages are excluded only after that window, a large conversation the user wrote most of but never acknowledged can report a count of 0 that is still capped. Acknowledging the conversation through what the user has seen restores an exact count.

SDK-backed lists refetch the inbox after an activity signal, coalesced into one refetch per 500 ms window (`activityRefreshWindowMs`), and immediately after a structural change. Every read advance is also an activity signal to every connected client of your app. In a very busy conversation with many viewers, `markReadOnReceive` acknowledges as messages arrive, and every acknowledgement that advances a viewer’s position is another signal to every client; if such a room dominates your traffic, set it to false there and acknowledge on load or explicitly instead.

Previews and unread counts need the 0.6.0 packages. Lists built with earlier SDK or UI releases (0.4 and 0.5) keep their creation order, show no previews or counts, and do not refetch on message activity.

### Mark unread

A user can mark a conversation unread to come back to it. The marker is private: it belongs to that user’s own membership, other members never see it, and it never appears in participant lists, webhooks or read events. It does not change the read position or `unreadCount`. Both READ and READ\_WRITE members can mark and clear their own conversations. The core SDKs expose `markConversationUnread` and `clearConversationUnread`; SDK-backed conversation lists expose `markUnread` and `clearUnread` on their controllers and ship no built-in row action, so wire the gesture your product wants through a custom row, menu or the controller.

Every inbox entry carries `isUnread`, `unreadMarkedAt` and `privateStateVersion`. `isUnread` is true when the count is above 0, when the count is capped, or when the marker is set. The default UI keeps the numeric badge for a count or a capped count, and renders a numberless dot named `Unread` for a conversation marked unread with nothing new: a dot, not an invented count. A custom row should apply the same rule.

Reading clears the marker only when the read reflects an intention newer than the mark. `privateStateVersion` advances on every mark and on every clear that removes a marker; a clear that finds nothing to remove changes nothing. An SDK-backed conversation captures it from the user’s own `membership` once, when the conversation opens, and sends it with every read acknowledgement of that opening; a later refresh of the same opening never re-reads it. The acknowledgement clears the marker only while the version is still current, so a mark made after the conversation was opened, from the list or from another device, survives that opening’s acknowledgements until the conversation is opened again. An acknowledgement without a version never clears a marker. A custom interface should capture the version at open the same way and pass it as `privateStateVersion` to `markConversationRead`.

A conversation with no messages has nothing to acknowledge. When it was opened with the marker set, SDK-backed conversations call `clearConversationUnread`with the captured version once per opening, under the same conditions and visibility rules as the load acknowledgement; a clear whose version no longer matches does nothing and is not an error. Custom interfaces can send the version alone to `markConversationRead` or call the conditional clear themselves.

A mark, a clear, or an acknowledgement that clears the marker raises the inbox-activity signal, so the user’s other devices refetch their inbox within the usual activity window, and an open conversation needs nothing. Each is one more signal to every connected client of your app, like a read advance.

Marking unread needs the 0.7.0 packages and the current backend. Lists built with 0.6.0 ignore `isUnread` and keep showing counts; conversations built with 0.6.0 send no version, so their acknowledgements never clear a marker, and the `membership` field is absent from conversations loaded through an older backend.

### Edit and delete your own messages

A user can change the text of a message they sent, or delete it, while they are still an active READ\_WRITE member of the conversation. Only the author may do either: another member’s message answers 403, and so does a READ member’s own message. Pending messages are never editable. The core SDKs expose `editMessage` and `deleteMessage` as the author operations, separate from the administrative edit and delete your backend calls with the client secret. SDK-backed conversations offer both on the user’s own confirmed messages and own the edit mode; controlled views render the actions only when you pass the callbacks.

Every message carries `revision`: 0 when it was sent and one more for every content change since, whether made by its author or by your server (administrative edits that only replace attachments count too). A message is edited when `revision` is above 0; the default UI shows the label `Edited` beside the time of such a message, for any sender. Derive the label from the revision, never from the message timestamps, which change for other reasons. When rows for one message arrive from several sources, keep the higher revision and never let a lower one overwrite it.

An edit sends the revision of the message as the user saw it, and the server applies it only while that revision is still current. When someone else, or the user’s other device, or your server, changed the message first, the edit answers `409` with code `REVISION_CONFLICT` and nothing changes. SDK-backed UI then reloads the message once, shows the current content in the editing banner, keeps the user’s draft in the composer and reports the conflict through its error state; the next save carries the fresh revision. The same conflict state is entered without a request when a newer revision of the message arrives while it is being edited. A custom interface should reload the message with `getMessage`, show what changed and retry with its revision; a reload that answers 404 with code `MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND` means the message was deleted in the meantime.

An edit changes text only. Attachments are preserved on edit, exactly as they were; sending `null` (the default composer sends an empty field as null) clears the caption of a message that keeps at least one attachment, and a text-only message cannot be saved empty. Failed edits preserve drafts: entering edit mode keeps the unsent draft aside and prefills the message text without a typing update, a save that fails or conflicts leaves the edited text and edit mode in place, and cancelling or saving restores the unsent draft.

Deleting a message removes it and its attachments from the conversation for every member and cannot be undone; files already received or downloaded cannot be retracted, and stored files are reclaimed by the existing user or app deletion cleanup. Deleting is unconditional: no revision is compared. Nothing is removed optimistically: SDK-backed UI removes the row once the server confirms, or answers 404 with code `MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND` because the message was already gone; any other failure keeps the row and reports the error. The deleting device then ignores late responses and updates for that message, so a slow history page or a late edit response never brings a deleted message back.

Other devices learn about an edit through the conversation’s message update, which carries the new revision, and through the inbox-activity signal, so previews refresh within the usual activity window without moving the conversation. They learn about a deletion through the room’s deletion notification and the inbox-change signal, which recalculates the preview and the position. A message deleted on one device is removed on the others without a refresh, and an edit in progress on one of them ends.

Editing and deleting need the 0.8.0 packages and the current backend. Clients built with 0.7.0 ignore `revision`: they show no Edited label and offer no actions, but still apply edits and deletions made elsewhere. Clients built with 0.8.0 need the 0.8 backend for the author endpoints; against an older backend a save or delete fails without removing anything, the draft stays, and every message reads as revision 0.

### React to a message

Active READ and READ\_WRITE members can view reactions. Only READ\_WRITE members can add or remove their own. The core SDKs expose `addReaction`, `removeReaction`, `getReactionSummaries`, and `listReactionUsers`. Adding an existing reaction or removing an absent one succeeds without changing anything. A deleted, inaccessible, or cross-app message returns `404 MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND`.

An emoji is one exact Unicode emoji sequence. Skin tones, flags, keycaps, and joined emoji count as one; `👍` and `👍🏽` are different reactions. Plain text and multiple emoji in one value are rejected. Summaries return at most 20 emoji per message, sorted by count, then emoji, with `hasMore` when additional types are hidden. Reactor lists use an opaque cursor; pass `nextCursor` back to load the next page.

SDK-backed conversation UI loads summaries for visible messages, refreshes a message after its private `reaction_changed` signal, and reconciles visible messages after reconnect. The signal contains IDs rather than reactor identities. Controlled views use the summaries and callbacks you provide. Custom rows can use their message context to render the library reaction bar, picker, and paginated reactor list. Reactions require a reaction-capable SDK, UI package, and backend.

### Quote a message in your reply

A reply carries a reference, not a copy. Sending with `replyToMessageId` stores the quoted message’s ID on the new message, and every message row carries that key: the quoted message’s ID, or `null` when the message is not a reply. The quoted message must be in the same conversation. A target in another room, one the sender cannot see, or one that no longer exists fails with `404` and code `MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND`, so a quote can never pull content out of a conversation the sender is not a member of.

The reference is written once, when the message is sent, and never changes. An edit changes text only and never moves what a reply points at, whether the edit is made by the author or by your server; an edit request that carries `replyToMessageId` at all is refused with `400` and code `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. A retry of the same send must repeat the same target: the quoted message is part of the content a `clientMessageId` stands for, so a retry that changes it answers `409`, while an identical retry returns the original message even when the quoted message has been deleted in the meantime.

Quoted text is re-read, never copied. SDK-backed UI resolves the quoted messages of a whole rendered page in one request and shows the author and the first 500 characters of the quoted text above the reply; a quoted message that is already on screen is taken from what is loaded and costs no request. Because the text is re-read, editing a quoted message updates every quote of it without a reload, and a quote never shows content the reader could not otherwise see. Custom interfaces should do the same: one batched resolution per rendered page with the distinct references on screen, never one request per row.

There are three display states and no fourth. A resolved quote shows the author and the quoted text. A reference a successful resolution returned nothing for means the quoted message is gone: keep the reply and its reference and show `Original message unavailable`. A reference that is not resolved yet shows the reference with no quoted text, never the unavailable wording, which would claim a deletion that has not happened. Absence from a successful resolution is the only deletion signal, and it is final; a failed request resolves nothing at all and is retried on the next page, reconciliation or burst of new messages.

Deleting a quoted message never deletes its replies and never erases the reference. The replies stay where they are, their quoted blocks become `Original message unavailable`, and their authors can still edit and delete them as usual.

Activating a quote opens the message it points at. When that message is already loaded, the conversation scrolls to it, moves focus to it and highlights it for about two seconds. When it is further back than the loaded range, SDK-backed UI loads a bounded window around it and replaces the loaded range with that window instead of downloading everything in between. A window is not the live conversation: while one is open, new messages are recorded but not shown, no read is reported, and the conversation offers a way back to the latest, which reloads the newest messages and shows everything that arrived meanwhile. Edits and deletions of messages inside the window still apply while it is open, and sending returns to the latest first, keeping the draft and the quote.

Quoting needs the 0.9.0 packages and the current backend. Clients built with 0.8.0 ignore `replyToMessageId`: they show no quoted block and offer no reply action, but still receive and show the replies other people send. Clients built with 0.9.0 need the 0.9 backend for the quoted-message and window requests; an older backend answers those two requests with a 404 that carries no code, which is never proof that a message is gone, so quoted blocks stay unresolved instead of becoming `Original message unavailable`, and the quote and jump affordances are hidden for the rest of the session instead of failing on every page. Sending a quote to an older backend is the one case that degrades silently: the backend keeps the message and drops the reference, so the quote shows while the message is pending and disappears when it is confirmed. Nothing is lost but the reference, and no second request could detect it, so move the backend before the clients.

### Retry a send without creating a duplicate

The core SDK generates `clientMessageId` when it is omitted. For a custom optimistic interface, call `createClientMessageId()` before displaying the pending message and pass that ID to the send call.

Reuse the same ID and payload when retrying the same send in the same conversation. For example, if the connection drops after sending “Hello”, retry with its original ID—not a new one. An accepted identical retry returns the existing message; changing its content with that ID returns `409`.

A separate intentional message needs a new ID, even if its text is identical. SDK-backed UI reconciles its pending messages with confirmations automatically. Custom UI should match by ID, sender, and conversation, not by message text.

### Keep a custom inbox up to date

SDK-backed lists handle refreshes automatically. If you own the inbox state, subscribe to the core SDK’s two inbox signals and reload the user’s inbox. Both are refresh signals, not conversation records. The inbox-change signal covers membership, conversation metadata, member profiles and deletions, and is also raised after every verified connection; reload immediately.

-   JavaScript: `realtime.onInboxChanged(clientId, handler)`
-   Flutter: `ConvoKit.realtime.onInboxChanged(ConvoKit.clientId)`
-   Android: `realtime.onInboxChanged(clientId)`
-   Swift: `realtime.onInboxChanged(appId: clientId)`

The inbox-activity signal covers a message sent or edited, a read position advancing, and the user’s own unread marker changing anywhere in the app. It is never raised on connection and reaches every connected client, so throttle the reload it triggers.

-   JavaScript: `realtime.onInboxActivity(clientId, handler)`
-   Flutter: `ConvoKit.realtime.onInboxActivity(ConvoKit.clientId)`
-   Android: `realtime.onInboxActivity(clientId)`
-   Swift: `realtime.onInboxActivity(appId: clientId)`

Subscribe after connecting the user, handle connection errors, and dispose listeners with their owning screen or session. After a reconnect, reload data your custom interface owns instead of assuming every event was received while offline.

### Attachments and access

Use the SDK upload helper, then include its returned URL in the message’s media. Default UI can show images and file cards; your app supplies file selection and opening or downloading behavior. Protected attachments require an authenticated user.

A conversation ID alone does not grant access. Your backend decides who can join. READ members may receive messages and report reads; sending messages, editing or deleting your own messages, typing, and uploading conversation media require READ\_WRITE access.

When a session expires permanently, sign in again and create fresh session-owned UI. If access to a room is removed, stop displaying its cached data. Removing access cannot retract messages or files already received or downloaded.

guides.text:
API reference

# REST API reference.

Call Admin routes from your backend with app credentials. Call SDK routes as an authenticated app user with a user token.

Base URL: `https://api.convokit.app`. Realtime connections and attachment uploads are handled by the [official SDKs](https://convokit.app/docs/sdks); their platform guides show the relevant methods.

Search API routes

26 endpoints

### Admin API

Call these routes from your backend. They require the app client secret and should never be called from browser or mobile code.

Admin`POST``/api/v1/auth/token`

### Issue a user token

Exchange app credentials for a short-lived token that represents one app user. The client uses this token for SDK routes.

### Headers

`x-client-id`string

**Required.** The app client ID from the dashboard.

`x-client-secret`string

**Required.** The app client secret. Keep this on your backend only.

### Body

`appUserId`string

**Required.** The ConvoKit app user ID to authorize.

### Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...",
    "expiresIn": 3600
  }
}
```

### cURL

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.convokit.app/api/v1/auth/token \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -H "x-client-id: $CONVOKIT_CLIENT_ID" \
  -H "x-client-secret: $CONVOKIT_CLIENT_SECRET" \
  -d '{"appUserId":"user_123"}'
```

Admin`POST``/api/v1/user`

### Create an app user

Create or sync a product user into ConvoKit before issuing tokens or adding the user to conversations.

### Headers

`x-client-id`string

**Required.** The app client ID from the dashboard.

`x-client-secret`string

**Required.** The app client secret. Keep this on your backend only.

### Body

`id`string

**Required.** A stable product user ID.

`name`string

Display name shown in conversations and the dashboard.

`imageUrl`string

Optional avatar URL.

### Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "user_123",
    "name": "Avery Stone",
    "imageUrl": null
  }
}
```

### cURL

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.convokit.app/api/v1/user \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -H "x-client-id: $CONVOKIT_CLIENT_ID" \
  -H "x-client-secret: $CONVOKIT_CLIENT_SECRET" \
  -d '{"id":"user_123","name":"Avery Stone"}'
```

### Edit a message

Update message content for moderation, correction, or administrative workflows: the administrative edit of any message in the app, separate from the author’s own edit (PATCH /api/v1/messages/:id/own). Supply text, media, or both; an omitted field keeps its current value, supplied media replace the message’s attachments, and the result must keep text or at least one media item (400 otherwise). Every successful update, media-only updates included, increments the message’s revision by exactly one, which is how clients label the message Edited. revision is optional: when present, the update is applied only while the stored revision still equals it, so an operator can refuse to overwrite an edit made since the message was loaded; a mismatch returns 409 with code REVISION\_CONFLICT and changes nothing, and a revision that is present but not an integer from 0 to 2147483647 returns 400 with code INVALID\_ARGUMENT before anything else is checked. Omit it to update unconditionally. A message that does not exist in this app receives 404 "Message not found". An edit never changes what a reply quotes: replyToMessageId is set once, when the message is sent, and a body that carries it at all returns 400 "reply target cannot be changed" with code INVALID\_ARGUMENT. The response is the updated message row with its attachments, its unchanged replyToMessageId and the incremented revision; other members receive the change as an update to the message in the open conversation plus one inbox\_activity signal.

SDK`GET``/api/v1/inbox`

### List the inbox

Return the current user’s inbox: one entry per conversation where they are an active participant, ordered by latest activity, with the latest message, an unread count and the caller’s own read state, so an inbox never has to fetch messages per conversation. Ordering uses the time of the latest surviving message, never earlier than the conversation’s creation time (an empty conversation sorts by its creation time), newest first; ties are broken by conversation ID. Editing a message changes the preview but does not move the conversation; deleting the latest message recalculates both the preview and the position. unreadCount counts surviving messages from other users after the caller’s read position (own messages never count). It is exact up to 1,000: when more than 1,000 messages follow the position, unreadCount is a lower bound over the first 1,000 and unreadCountCapped is true. isUnread is the badge predicate: true when unreadCount is above 0, when the count is capped, or when the caller marked the conversation unread; unreadMarkedAt is when they marked it (null while no marker is set) and privateStateVersion is the version of that private state (see POST /api/v1/conversations/:id/unread). A marked conversation with nothing new therefore reports isUnread true with unreadCount 0: render a dot, not an invented count. These three fields, like readPosition and lastReadAt, are the caller’s own; other members never see the marker. Pages are addressed by an opaque cursor: pass nextCursor back as cursor until it is null. A cursor stays valid after its conversation moves or is deleted; offset is not accepted and returns 400 with code INVALID\_ARGUMENT. One response is internally consistent; across pages, refresh from the first page and de-duplicate by conversation ID, keeping the later entry. conversation has the GET /api/v1/conversations shape with participants limited to at most 10 members (you, the sender of the latest message when still a member, then active members by ID); latestMessage has the GET /api/v1/messages row shape with at most its first 4 attachments, or null for an empty conversation. A malformed limit returns 400 with code INVALID\_ARGUMENT; a cursor ConvoKit did not issue returns 400 with code INVALID\_CURSOR.

SDK`POST``/api/v1/conversations/:id/read`

### Mark a conversation read

Record how far the current user has read a conversation. A read is a position, not a timestamp: ConvoKit stores the message named by throughMessageId as the position, so a request that arrives after a newer message does not mark that newer message read. Without throughMessageId the position becomes the newest message on the server at request time. Positions never move backward; an older target after a newer one is accepted without changing the position. Both READ and READ\_WRITE members can report reads. Success returns 204 with no body. A caller who is not an active member receives 404 "Conversation not found"; a throughMessageId that is not a message in this conversation receives 404 with code MESSAGE\_NOT\_FOUND; a throughMessageId that is not a string receives 400. Without a target in a conversation that has no messages, the request still returns 204: lastReadAt advances and readPosition stays null. When the position advances, other members receive a read realtime event carrying userId, readAt, and readPosition. privateStateVersion is optional: the version of the caller’s private unread state captured when the conversation was opened (membership.privateStateVersion on GET /api/v1/conversations/:id). When it equals the current version, the same acknowledgement also clears the caller’s unread marker; when it is absent or no longer matches, the marker is left alone and the position still advances as usual, so a mark-unread issued after the conversation was opened survives a late acknowledgement. A body with only privateStateVersion acknowledges like the no-target form, so it clears the marker of a conversation that has no messages without naming one. A privateStateVersion that is present but not an integer from 0 to 2147483647 receives 400 with code INVALID\_ARGUMENT. The marker never appears in the read event, and clearing it alone sends no read event.

SDK`PATCH``/api/v1/messages/:id/own`

### Edit your own message

Replace the text of a message the current user sent. Only the author may edit, and only while still an active READ\_WRITE member of the conversation; this is the author’s edit, separate from the administrative PATCH /api/v1/messages/:id your backend calls with the client secret. The body always carries both keys: text is the new text or null, and revision is the revision of the message as the user saw it. Text is trimmed and an empty string is stored as null; null is accepted only while the message keeps at least one attachment (it clears the caption), otherwise the request returns 400 "A message must have text or at least one media item". Attachments are never changed by this request, and neither is what the message quotes: replyToMessageId is set once, when the message is sent, so a body that carries it at all returns 400 "reply target cannot be changed" with code INVALID\_ARGUMENT. The edit is applied only while the stored revision still equals the one sent; success returns 200 with the updated row, whose revision is one higher, and other members receive the change as an update to the message in the open conversation plus one inbox\_activity signal (the conversation does not move in the inbox). When the message was edited in the meantime, by another device or by your server, the request returns 409 with code REVISION\_CONFLICT and changes nothing: reload the message and retry with its revision. A missing text returns 400 "text is required" and a text that is neither a string nor null returns 400 "text must be a string or null", both with code INVALID\_ARGUMENT; a revision that is missing or not an integer from 0 to 2147483647 returns 400 "revision must be an integer between 0 and 2147483647" with code INVALID\_ARGUMENT. These are decided before anything else, so a malformed body is a 400 for outsiders too. A member who did not send the message, and a READ member, receive 403 "Insufficient permissions". A message that does not exist, belongs to another app, was deleted, or is in a conversation the caller is not an active member of receives one 404 body with code MESSAGE\_NOT\_FOUND; treat only that coded 404 as the message being gone, because a backend without this route answers a 404 without a JSON code.

Files already received or downloaded cannot be retracted, and stored files are reclaimed by the existing user or app deletion cleanup rather than by this request. Success returns 200 with the deleted ID. A member who did not send the message, and a READ member, receive 403 "Insufficient permissions". A message that does not exist, belongs to another app, was already deleted, or is in a conversation the caller is not an active member of receives one 404 body with code MESSAGE\_NOT\_FOUND; treat only that coded 404 as the message being gone.

### Headers

`x-client-id`string

**Required.** The app client ID from the dashboard.

`authorization`Bearer token

**Required.** A scoped ConvoKit user token issued by your backend.

### Path params

`id`string

**Required.** The message ID. The caller must be its author and an active READ\_WRITE member of its conversation.

### Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "message_123"
  }
}
```

### cURL

```bash
curl -X DELETE https://api.convokit.app/api/v1/messages/message_123/own \
  -H "x-client-id: $CONVOKIT_CLIENT_ID" \
  -H "authorization: Bearer $CONVOKIT_USER_TOKEN"
```

### Permission and not found responses

```json
// 403: the caller did not send the message, or is a READ member
{ "error": "Insufficient permissions" }

// 404: unknown, already deleted, in another app, or in a conversation the caller cannot access
{ "error": "Message not found", "code": "MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND" }
```

### Realtime events

Conversation-level events (new messages, typing, read receipts) and app-wide presence are described in each SDK guide. Two app-wide signals keep an inbox fresh. Both are empty: they carry no conversation IDs or contents, and each client refetches only its own inbox through `GET /api/v1/inbox`. Expect one `inbox_activity` per message sent or edited plus one per viewer whose read position advances, plus one per private mark or clear, delivered to every connected client of the app, so throttle the refetch it triggers and refetch immediately on `inbox_changed`. A private unread marker stays private: it never appears in participant lists, webhooks or `read` events, and the signal only tells the marking user’s other devices to refetch. An edit of a message, by its author or by your server, reaches an open conversation as an update to that message carrying its new `revision`, and every other client through `inbox_activity`; a deletion reaches an open conversation as the room’s deletion notification for the message ID, and every other client through `inbox_changed`. A reply is an ordinary new message and reaches an open conversation the same way any message does, carrying the ID of the message it quotes and no quoted text; resolve the quoted text with `GET /api/v1/conversations/:id/reply-previews` for the whole rendered page rather than once per reply. One inbox response is internally consistent; across pages, refresh from the first page and de-duplicate by conversation ID.

| Event | Sent after | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `inbox_changed` | A structural change to one of the user’s conversations: membership (a member added, removed, leaving, rejoining, archiving or changing role), conversation metadata (created, renamed, or a new description or image), a member’s profile, or a deletion, including a deleted message. | Refetch your inbox immediately. The SDKs also raise it after every verified connection or reconnection, so a custom inbox reloads what it may have missed while offline. |
| `inbox_activity` | A message sent or edited, a member’s read position advancing, or your own unread marker changing (mark, clear, or an acknowledgement that clears it), in any conversation of the app. Acknowledgements that do not advance a position or clear your own unread marker, presence, and message deletions do not send it. | Refetch your inbox to refresh previews, unread counts and your own unread marker, throttled: the SDK-backed UI libraries wait up to 500 ms and refetch once per window. It is never raised on connection, and an open conversation does not need it. |

})` (returning `ClearUnreadResult`); the default adapter does. - Without them `markUnread` and `clearUnread` reject, and an empty room keeps its marker. - For editing and deleting, the adapter may implement the optional `editMessage?(messageId, { text, revision })` (resolving with the updated core `Message`; reject a stale revision with `status: 409` and `code: 'REVISION_CONFLICT'`, a gone message with `code: 'MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND'`) and `deleteMessage?(messageId)`; the default adapter forwards both to the core's author calls. - Without them no action renders and `saveEdit` / `deleteMessage` reject; existing adapter literals keep compiling. - `EditMessageInput` is re-exported. `ConversationList``Conversation`SDK-backed loading, pagination, previews, unread counts and the private unread marker, sending, editing and deleting your own messages, typing, and read state. `ConversationListView``ConversationView``MessageListView`Presentation controlled entirely by your application state and callbacks. ### Plug-and-play React integration Connect the browser-safe core client, adapt it once, render the inbox, then open the selected room by ID. `ConversationListView` accepts both, and `renderConversationItem` receives `summary` and `currentUserId` (absent means the previous rows and no `You:` prefix). - Rows arrive in inbox order and pages are merged by conversation ID with the later entry winning, re-sorted by activity, then ID. - Activity signals are coalesced into one refetch per `activityRefreshWindowMs` (default 500; 0 refetches on every signal), while membership and metadata changes refetch immediately. - If the inbox route answers 404, the list falls back to conversation paging without previews for the rest of the session; the next login tries again. ```tsx import { ConversationListView, inboxPreviewText, useConversationList } from '@convokitapp/react-ui' const list = useConversationList({ client: uiClient, activityRefreshWindowMs: 500, // default; 0 refetches on every activity signal }) setRoomId(room.id)} renderConversationItem={({ conversation, summary, currentUserId, onSelect }) => ( )} /> ``` ### Mark unread - `useConversationList` and the `ConversationList` controller expose `markUnread(conversationId)` and `clearUnread(conversationId, { ifVersion? })`. - The marker is private to the viewer: other members, webhooks and read events never see it, and `unreadCount` is untouched. - `clearUnread` resolves with the server's `cleared` (this request removed a marker), not with whether the room is read; an unmarked room or a stale `ifVersion` resolves `false` without an error. - After either response the row's current summary takes `unreadMarkedAt` and `privateStateVersion` as one unit and `isUnread` is recomputed, only while the response is not older than the stored version, so a delayed response never brings back a marker a newer action removed; failures surface through `error` without evicting rows. - Every `InboxSummary` carries `isUnread`, `unreadMarkedAt` and `privateStateVersion`. - A row is unread (`data-unread`, bold title) when `isUnread`, the count is above 0, or the count is capped; a count or a capped count keeps the numeric badge, and a room unread only through the marker renders a numberless dot, `.ckui-badge.ckui-badge--dot`, with `role="img"` and the accessible name `Unread`, never an invented count. - There is no built-in row action: wire it through `renderConversationItem`, a menu or `onControllerChange`. - SDK-backed rooms capture the viewer's own `membership.privateStateVersion` once, the first time the room opens (also after a transient first-load failure), never from a later refresh, and send it with every acknowledgement of that open, so reading clears the marker only while the version is still current and a mark made after the open survives until the room is reopened. - A room opened with the marker and nothing rendered calls the adapter's `clearConversationUnread` with the captured version once per open, beside its unchanged untargeted acknowledgement, under the same conditions and visibility gating as the load acknowledgement; `cleared: false` is not an error. - Marker changes on other devices arrive through the throttled activity refetch. - Lists built with the previous release ignore `isUnread` and keep their counts. ```tsx const list = useConversationList({ client: uiClient }) // No built-in row action: call the controller from a custom row, a menu, or // the controller you receive through onControllerChange. setRoomId(room.id)} renderConversationItem={({ conversation, summary, onSelect }) => (
)} /> // Remove the marker without opening the room, only while it still has the // version the row shows. Resolves the server's cleared: false is not an error. const cleared = await list.clearUnread(conversation.id, { ifVersion: summary.privateStateVersion }) // SDK-backed rooms capture membership.privateStateVersion when they open and // send it with every acknowledgement of that open; nothing to wire. ``` ### Edit and delete your own messages - `useConversation` and the `Conversation` controller expose `editingMessage` (the message being edited, as the viewer saw it when editing began; `null` outside edit mode), `canEditMessages` / `canDeleteMessages` (whether the adapter implements the members), `startEditing(messageId)`, `cancelEditing()`, `saveEdit(text)` and `deleteMessage(messageId)` (both resolve a boolean). - `startEditing` is a no-op for another member's row, a pending row, a removed row, a `READ` role or an adapter without `editMessage`; it sends nothing, not even a typing update. - `saveEdit` trims the text and sends the revision captured when editing began, never the live row's, so the server compares against what the viewer saw. - A stale revision (409 `REVISION_CONFLICT`) reloads the row once through `getMessage`: the row shows the current content, the snapshot moves to it so the banner shows what changed and the next save carries the fresh revision, `error` carries the conflict and the edited text stays in the composer. - The same state is entered without a request when a newer revision of the edited row arrives while editing. - A 404 with code `MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND` on the save or the reload removes the row and ends edit mode; any other failure (403, network, a 500, or an uncoded 404 from an older backend) keeps the row, the draft and edit mode and surfaces through `error` without evicting history. - `deleteMessage` is never optimistic: the row goes once the server confirms or answers `MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND`, and stays on any other failure; late responses and updates for a removed row are dropped, and a removal by any path ends edit mode on it. - When rows for one message meet, the higher `revision` wins and a lower one never overwrites; equal revisions keep the timestamp rule. - Default rows: eligible rows (the viewer's own, confirmed, role not `READ`, callback present) render `.ckui-message-actions` with `Edit message` and `Delete message` buttons, always in the DOM. - The only rule concealing them (`opacity: 0` and `pointer-events: none`) lives inside `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` and is lifted on `.ckui-message-row:hover` / `:focus-within`, so touch and keyboard users always see them; never pending rows) show `.ckui-message-edited` with the text and accessible name `Edited` beside the time, for any sender. - Rows that are not eligible render exactly as before. - Default composer: while `editingMessage` is set a `role="status"` banner reads `Editing message` with the original text and a visible `Cancel` named `Cancel editing`; the field is prefilled with the message text once, silently, after the unsent draft is stashed; the primary action becomes a check icon named `Save message` (`Send message` otherwise) and is enabled when the trimmed field is non-empty or the row has attachments, so saving an empty field on a message with attachments sends `text: null` and clears the caption while every attachment stays; a text-only message can never be saved empty. - Enter saves, Escape cancels; the field is never cleared during a save; success, Cancel and Escape restore the stash (emitting `onTypingChange` for a non-empty one); if the row is removed while editing, text you changed stays and an untouched or emptied field gets the stash back. - The single `send` each view hands to its composer saves while editing, so custom composers need no branching; they additionally receive `editing?: { message, cancel }`. - Controlled views: `ConversationView` accepts `editingMessage`, `onEditMessage(message)`, `onSaveEdit(message, text)` (`false` keeps edit mode and the text, like `onSendMessage`), `onCancelEdit()`, `onDeleteMessage(message)`, `canEditMessage(message)` (an override of the own-and-writable rule for both actions; pending rows stay ineligible) and `confirmDelete`; `MessageListView` accepts `onEditMessage`, `onDeleteMessage`, `canEditMessage` and `confirmDelete`. - Without the callbacks the markup is byte-identical to the previous release. - `renderMessage` receives `isEdited`, `canEdit`, `canDelete` and, exactly when the action is available, `edit()` and `remove()` (which asks `confirmDelete` when given, then calls `onDeleteMessage`). - The bound `Conversation` wires the controller only when the adapter supports the action and passes `canEditMessage` / `confirmDelete` through. - Deleting a message removes it and its attachments from the conversation for every member and cannot be undone; files already received or downloaded cannot be retracted. - Consumer-built `Message` literals gain the required `revision` member. - Clients built with the previous release ignore `revision` and show no actions; against an older backend the author calls answer an uncoded 404 that surfaces through `error` without removing anything, and every row reads as revision 0. ```tsx // SDK-backed: own confirmed rows offer Edit message / Delete message, the // composer saves while editing, and confirmDelete replaces the inline prompt. window.confirm(`Delete "${message.text ?? 'this message'}"?`)} /> // Controlled: edit mode is a pure function of editingMessage and the callbacks. // Leave them out and no action renders. const room = useConversation({ client: uiClient, conversationId: roomId }) (await room.sendMessage({ text })) !== null} readPositionByUserId={room.readPositionByUserId} editingMessage={room.editingMessage} onEditMessage={(message) => room.startEditing(message.id)} onSaveEdit={(_message, text) => room.saveEdit(text)} onCancelEdit={room.cancelEditing} onDeleteMessage={(message) => room.deleteMessage(message.id)} error={room.error} renderMessage={({ message, isEdited, edit, remove }) => (
{message.text} {isEdited ? (edited) : null} {edit ? : null} {remove ? : null}
)} renderComposer={({ value, setValue, send, editing }) => (

(`--ckui-badge`). - `useConversationList` exposes `summaries` (a map from conversation ID to `InboxSummary`) and `currentUserId` as readonly refs; `ConversationListView` accepts both, and the `#conversation-item` slot receives `summary` and `currentUserId` (absent means the previous rows and no `You:` prefix). - Rows arrive in inbox order and pages are merged by conversation ID with the later entry winning, re-sorted by activity, then ID. - Activity signals are coalesced into one refetch per `activityRefreshWindowMs` (default 500; 0 refetches on every signal), while membership and metadata changes refetch immediately. - If the inbox route answers 404, the list falls back to conversation paging without previews for the rest of its life; a new list, for example after the next login, tries again. ```html ``` ### Mark unread - `useConversationList` and the `ConversationList` controller expose `markUnread(conversationId)` and `clearUnread(conversationId, { ifVersion? })`. - The marker is private to the viewer: other members, webhooks and read events never see it, and `unreadCount` is untouched. - `clearUnread` resolves with the server's `cleared` (this request removed a marker), not with whether the room is read; an unmarked room or a stale `ifVersion` resolves `false` without an error. - After either response the row's current summary takes `unreadMarkedAt` and `privateStateVersion` as one unit and `isUnread` is recomputed, only while the response is not older than the stored version, so a delayed response never brings back a marker a newer action removed; `.ckui-unread-badge.ckui-unread-badge--dot`, with `role="img"` and the accessible name `Unread`, never an invented count. - There is no built-in row action: wire it through the `#conversation-item` slot, a menu or `onControllerChange`. - SDK-backed rooms capture the viewer's own `membership.privateStateVersion` once, the first time the room opens (also after a transient first-load failure), never from a later refresh, and send it with every acknowledgement of that open, so reading clears the marker only while the version is still current and a mark made after the open survives until the room is reopened. - A room opened with the marker and nothing rendered calls the adapter's `clearConversationUnread` with the captured version once per open, under the same conditions and visibility gating as the load acknowledgement; `cleared: false` is not an error. - Marker changes on other devices arrive through the throttled activity refetch. - Lists built with the previous release ignore `isUnread` and keep their counts. ```html ``` ### Edit and delete your own messages - `useConversation` and the `Conversation` controller expose `editingMessage` (the message being edited, as the viewer saw it when editing began; `null` outside edit mode), `canEditMessages` / `canDeleteMessages` (whether the adapter implements the members), `startEditing(messageId)`, `cancelEditing()`, `saveEdit(text)` and `deleteMessage(messageId)` (both resolve a boolean; the composable exposes the state as readonly refs). - `startEditing` is a no-op for another member's row, a pending row, a removed row, a `READ` role or an adapter without `editMessage`; it sends nothing, not even a typing update. - `saveEdit` trims the text and sends the revision captured when editing began, never the live row's, so the server compares against what the viewer saw. - A stale revision (409 `REVISION_CONFLICT`) reloads the row once through `getMessage`: the row shows the current content, the snapshot moves to it so the banner shows what changed and the next save carries the fresh revision, `error` carries the conflict and the edited text stays in the composer. - The same state is entered without a request when a newer revision of the edited row arrives while editing. - A 404 with code `MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND` on the save or the reload removes the row and ends edit mode; any other failure (403, network, a 500, or an uncoded 404 from an older backend) keeps the row, the draft and edit mode and surfaces through `error` without evicting history. - `deleteMessage` is never optimistic: the row goes once the server confirms or answers `MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND`, and stays on any other failure; late responses and updates for a removed row are dropped, and a removal by any path ends edit mode on it. - When rows for one message meet, the higher `revision` wins and a lower one never overwrites; equal revisions keep the timestamp rule. - Default rows: eligible rows (the viewer's own, confirmed, role not `READ`, callback present) render `.ckui-message-actions` with `Edit message` and `Delete message` buttons, always in the DOM. - The only rule concealing them (`opacity: 0` and `pointer-events: none`) lives inside `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` and is lifted on `.ckui-message-row:hover` / `:focus-within`, so touch and keyboard users always see them; never `display: none`. - `Delete message` opens an inline `role="group"` named `Delete this message?` with `Delete` (accessible name `Confirm delete`) and `Cancel` (`Cancel delete`); pass `confirmDelete(message)` to use your own dialog. - Rows whose content changed after the send (`revision` above 0; never pending rows) show `.ckui-message-edited` with the text and accessible name `Edited` beside the time, for any sender. - Rows that are not eligible render exactly as before. - Default composer: while `editingMessage` is set a `role="status"` banner (`.ckui-composer__editing`) reads `Editing message` with the original text and a visible `Cancel` named `Cancel editing`; the field is prefilled with the message text once, silently, after the unsent draft is stashed; the primary action becomes a check icon named `Save message` (`Send message` otherwise) and is enabled when the trimmed field is non-empty or the row has attachments, so saving an empty field on a message with attachments sends `text: null` and clears the caption while every attachment stays; a text-only message can never be saved empty. - Enter saves, Escape cancels; the field is never cleared during a save; success, Cancel and Escape restore the stash (emitting `onTypingChange` for a non-empty one); if the row is removed while editing, text you changed stays and an untouched or emptied field gets the stash back. - The single `send` each view hands to its composer saves while editing, so custom composers need no branching; `#composer` slots additionally receive `editing` (the message) and `cancelEdit` while editing. - Controlled views: `ConversationView` accepts `editingMessage`, `onEditMessage(message)`, `onSaveEdit(message, text)` (`false` keeps edit mode and the text, like `onSendMessage`), `onCancelEdit()`, `onDeleteMessage(message)`, `canEditMessage(message)` (an override of the own-and-writable rule for both actions; pending rows stay ineligible) and `confirmDelete`, also as the `@edit-message`, byte-identical to the previous release. - `#message` slots receive `isEdited`, `canEdit`, `canDelete` and, exactly when the action is available, `edit()` and `remove()` (which asks `confirmDelete` when given, otherwise deletes at once: a custom row owns its own prompt). - The bound `Conversation` wires the composable only when the adapter supports the action, forwards `canEditMessage` / `confirmDelete` and emits the four events. - Deleting a message removes it and its attachments from the conversation for every member and cannot be undone; files already received or downloaded cannot SwiftUI SDK

# Ship native iOS chat quickly, then replace exactly the views your product owns.

ConvoKitUI adds SDK-backed and controlled SwiftUI components, inbox previews and unread counts, protected media, durable and live read receipts, realtime typing, pagination, themes, density presets, and replaceable view closures.

Published`ConvoKitUI 0.10.1``ConvoKit 0.10.1`

### Native iOS defaults with application-level ownership

-   Use semantic system colors, native List selection, and standard SwiftUI navigation.
-   Start with controller-backed components, or use controlled views when your app owns state, analytics, caching, and navigation.
-   Version 0.10.1 anchors compact reaction chips and a quick emoji popover to messages, with a larger picker for custom emoji.

[Swift package](https://github.com/ConvoKitApp/ConvoKit-Swift-Package) [Public examples](https://github.com/ConvoKitApp/ConvoKit-Swift-UI-Examples)

### Install both products

iOS 15+ through the public binary Swift package.

```swift
dependencies: [
    .package(
        url: "https://github.com/ConvoKitApp/ConvoKit-Swift-Package",
        exact: "0.10.1"
    )
]

// Add both ConvoKit and ConvoKitUI to your iOS app target.
```

### Choose the ownership layer

Both layers share the same native components and customization hooks.

`ConvoKitConversationList``ConvoKitConversation`Network loading, pagination, previews, unread counts and the private unread marker, sending, editing and deleting your own messages, protected images, typing, receipts, and realtime included.

`ConversationListView``ConversationView`Presentation-only SwiftUI views driven by your observable state and callbacks.

### Render a list and selected room

Pass one connected ConvoKitClient into the SDK-backed views.

```swift
ConvoKitConversationList(
    client: convoKit,
    pageSize: 30,
    selectedConversationId: selectedRoomId,
    onSelect: { selectedRoomId = $0.id }
)

if let roomId = selectedRoomId,
   let chat = try? ConvoKitConversation(
        client: convoKit,
        conversationId: roomId,
        onAddAttachment: openAttachmentPicker,
        onOpenMedia: openMedia
   ) {
    chat
}
```

iPhone simulator renders

### Controlled views and closures

Your app supplies state and replaces only its product-specific views.

```swift
ConversationView(
    conversation: state.conversation,
    messages: state.messages,
    currentUserId: state.currentUserId,
    typingUserIds: state.typingUserIds,
    readAtByUserId: state.readAtByUserId,
    readPositionByUserId: state.readPositionByUserId,

    configuration: .init(showsReadReceipts: true),
```
