### Theme and density

Environment modifiers style the full subtree without global singletons.

```swift
let brandTheme = ConvoKitTheme(
    accent: .indigo,
    background: Color(.systemGroupedBackground),
    surface: Color(.secondarySystemBackground),
    incomingBubble: Color.indigo.opacity(0.09),
    outgoingBubble: .indigo,
    cornerRadius: 18
)

ConvoKitConversation(client: convoKit, conversationId: roomId)
    .convoKitTheme(brandTheme)
    .convoKitDensity(.compact)
```

### Inbox previews and unread counts

-   The SDK-backed `ConvoKitConversationList` shows each room's latest message, its activity time in the viewer's timezone, and an unread badge.
-   The preview reads `You: …` for your own latest message, `Name: …` for a named sender in a room with more than two participants, and the body alone otherwise; a media-only message reads `Photo`, the file name or `File`, `Location`, or `Contact`.
-   The badge renders while `unreadCount` is above 0 or the count is capped, shows the count up to 99 and `99+` above that or whenever the count is capped, and carries the accessible name `N unread` (`99+ unread` when capped) with the visible label hidden from assistive clients; the title is bold while unread.
-   A room marked unread with a count of 0 renders a numberless dot instead (see Mark unread).
-   Its color is the `ConvoKitTheme.badge` token, which follows `accent` until set.
-   `ConversationListController` publishes `summaries` (conversation ID to `InboxSummary`) and `currentUserId`; `ConversationListView` gains an init overload with `summaries` and `currentUserId` (the existing init delegates with none, so existing call sites keep compiling), and `ConversationItemContext` gains `summary` and `currentUserId` for custom rows (absent means the previous rows and no `You:` prefix).
-   Rows arrive in inbox order and pages are merged by conversation ID with the later entry winning, re-sorted by activity, then ID; there is no comparator, so hosts that want another order sort `conversations` themselves for the controlled view.
-   Activity signals are coalesced into one refresh per `activityRefreshWindowMs` (500 ms for `ConvoKitConversationList` and the existing controller inits; the `ConversationListController(client:pageSize:activityRefreshWindowMs:)` overload takes it explicitly, 0 refreshes at once), while membership and metadata changes refresh immediately.
-   The list opens no per-room channels.
-   If the inbox route answers 404, the list falls back to conversation paging without previews until it is stopped and refreshed.
-   There is no public adapter protocol: custom state layers use the controlled view.

```swift
// SDK-backed: previews, times and unread badges come from the controller.
ConvoKitConversationList(client: convoKit, selectedConversationId: selectedRoomId) {
    selectedRoomId = $0.id
} row: { context in
    AnyView(HStack {
        Text(context.conversation.displayTitle)
        if let summary = context.summary, summary.unreadCount > 0 || summary.unreadCountCapped {
            Text(summary.unreadCountCapped || summary.unreadCount > 99 ? "99+" : String(summary.unreadCount))
                .accessibilityLabel(summary.unreadCountCapped ? "99+ unread" : "\(summary.unreadCount) unread")
        } else if context.summary?.isUnread == true {
            // Marked unread with nothing new: a dot, never an invented count.
            Circle().frame(width: 8, height: 8).accessibilityLabel("Unread")
        }
    })
}

// A controller you own takes the activity window explicitly (milliseconds; 0 refreshes at once).
let list = ConversationListController(client: convoKit, pageSize: 30, activityRefreshWindowMs: 500)

// Controlled: pass the same data to the view.
ConversationListView(
    conversations: list.conversations,
    summaries: list.summaries,
    currentUserId: list.currentUserId,
    onSelect: { selectedRoomId = $0.id }
)
```

### Mark unread

-   `ConversationListController` exposes `markUnread(_:)` and `clearUnread(_:ifVersion:) -> Bool`, and `ConvoKitConversationList` gains a trailing `onController: ((ConversationListController) -> Void)? = nil` parameter that receives the wrapper's controller once, before its first refresh (existing call sites keep compiling).
-   The marker is private to the bound user: other members, webhooks and read events never see it, and `unreadCount` is untouched.
-   `clearUnread` returns the server's `cleared` (this request removed a marker), not whether the room is read; an unmarked room or a stale `ifVersion` returns false without an error.
-   After either answer the row's current summary takes `unreadMarkedAt` and `privateStateVersion` as one unit and `isUnread` is recomputed, only while the answer is not older than the stored version, so a delayed answer never brings back a marker a newer action removed; failures surface through `error` without evicting rows, and a stopped list behind a detail view still patches its kept rows.
-   Every `InboxSummary` carries `isUnread`, `unreadMarkedAt` and `privateStateVersion` (trailing memberwise parameters with defaults, so existing literals keep compiling), and `loadMore()` keeps them across pages.
-   A row is unread (bold title) when `isUnread`, the count is above 0, or the count is capped; a count or a capped count keeps the numeric badge, and a room unread only through the marker renders a numberless 8-point dot filled with `ConvoKitTheme.badge` whose accessible name is `Unread`, never an invented count.
-   There is no built-in row affordance: wire a swipe action or context menu through a custom `row:` and `onController`.
-   SDK-backed rooms capture the user's own `membership.privateStateVersion` on every open, that is, every `refresh()` that activates the controller (the initial load and each re-appearance after `stop()`, which also resets the acknowledged floor so the newest rendered row is acknowledged again with the fresh version), never from a later reconcile, and send it with every acknowledgement of that open, so reading clears the marker only while the version is still current and a mark made after the open survives until the room is reopened.
-   A room opened with the marker and nothing rendered calls `clearConversationUnread` with the captured version once per open, under `markReadOnLoad` and the same visibility gating as the load acknowledgement; `cleared` false is not an error.
-   Marker changes on other devices arrive through the throttled activity refetch.
-   Lists built with the previous release ignore `isUnread` and keep their counts.

```swift
@State private var list: ConversationListController?

// No built-in row affordance: the trailing onController hands you the wrapper's
// controller once, before its first refresh, so a custom row can act on it.
ConvoKitConversationList(client: convoKit, selectedConversationId: selectedRoomId) {
    selectedRoomId = $0.id
} row: { context in
    AnyView(Text(context.conversation.displayTitle)
        .swipeActions {
            Button("Mark unread") {
                Task { await list?.markUnread(context.conversation.id) }
            }
        })
} onController: { list = $0 }

// Remove the marker without opening the room, only while it still has the
// version the row shows. Returns the server's cleared: false is not an error.
let cleared = await list?.clearUnread(conversation.id, ifVersion: summary.privateStateVersion)

// SDK-backed rooms capture membership.privateStateVersion on every open, that
// is, on every refresh() that activates the controller: the initial load and
// each re-appearance after stop(). Nothing to wire.
ConvoKitConversation(client: convoKit, conversationId: roomId)
```

### Edit and delete your own messages

-   `ConversationController` exposes `editingMessage` (the message being edited, as the user saw it when editing began; nil outside edit mode), `canEditMessages` / `canDeleteMessages` (a live session with a `READ_WRITE` membership), `startEditing(_ messageId:)`, `cancelEditing()`, `saveEdit(_ text:) -> Bool` and `deleteMessage(_ messageId:) -> Bool`.
-   `startEditing` is a no-op for another member's row, a pending, removed or unknown id, a `READ` membership or an inactive session; it sends nothing, not even a typing update.
-   `saveEdit` trims the text and sends the revision captured when editing began, never the live row's, so the server compares against what the user saw.
-   A stale revision (409 `REVISION_CONFLICT`) reloads the row exactly once through `getMessage`: the current row replaces the rendered row and the snapshot, so the banner shows what changed and the next save carries the fresh revision, `error` carries the conflict and the edited text stays in the composer.
-   The same state is entered without a request when a newer revision of the edited row arrives while editing.
-   A 404 with code `MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND` on the save or the reload removes the row and ends edit mode; any other failure (403, network, a server error, or an uncoded 404 from an older backend) keeps the row, the snapshot and edit mode and only sets `error`; an edit or a delete never retires the room.
-   `deleteMessage` removes nothing optimistically: on success, or when the server already answers `MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND`, the row and edit mode go, exactly like a `message_deleted` event, so late answers and updates for the id are dropped; other failures keep the row and set `error`.
-   When rows for one message meet, the higher `revision` wins and a lower one never overwrites; equal revisions keep the timestamp rule.
-   Default rows: an eligible row (`onEditMessage` given, the user's own, confirmed, `canSend`, role not `READ`) gains a context menu and the named accessibility actions `Edit message` / `Delete message`; the built-in confirmation dialog `Delete this message?` offers `Delete` / `Cancel` unless `confirmDelete` decides.
-   Every `isEdited` row shows `Edited` beside its time, for any sender; rows that are not eligible render exactly as before.
-   Default composer: while `editingMessage` is set a banner shows `Editing message` with the row's current text and a `Cancel` button (accessible name `Cancel editing`; Escape), the primary action becomes a checkmark named `Save message` (`Send message` otherwise), the attachment button is disabled, and Save is enabled when the trimmed field is non-empty or the edited row has attachments, so saving an empty field on a message with attachments sends a nil text and clears the caption while every attachment stays; a text-only message can never be saved empty.
-   Entering edit mode stashes the unsent draft and prefills the row's text without a typing update; the field is never cleared while a save is in flight; Cancel and a successful save restore the stash with the usual typing update; an external clear keeps text the user changed and restores the stash only when the field is empty or still the prefilled text.
-   Sending and saving share the one submit path.
-   Controlled view: `ConversationView` gains trailing defaulted `editingMessage: Message? = nil`, `onEditMessage:`, `onCancelEditing:`, `onSaveEdit:` (`(String) async -> Bool`; false keeps the text and edit mode), `onDeleteMessage:` (`(Message) async -> Bool`) and `confirmDelete:` (`@Sendable (Message) async -> Bool`); without them every row and the composer render exactly as before, and existing call sites keep compiling.
-   Custom `messageView:` renderers receive the additive `MessageContext.isEdited`, `canEdit`, `canDelete`, `edit` (enters edit mode) and `remove` (confirms, then deletes through `onDeleteMessage` and answers whether it did).
-   `ConvoKitConversation` wires the controller and gains trailing `confirmDelete:` and `onController: ((ConversationController) -> Void)? = nil`, which receives the wrapper's controller once, before its first `refresh()` (the list's pattern), so a custom row can drive it.
-   There is still no public adapter protocol.
-   Deleting a message removes it and its attachments from the conversation for every member and cannot be undone; files already received or downloaded cannot be retracted.
-   `Message.revision` has a memberwise default, so existing literals keep compiling.
-   Clients built with the previous release ignore `revision` and show no actions; against an older backend every row reads revision 0, no `Edited` label shows, and a save or delete fails with an uncoded 404 that keeps the row and edit mode.

```swift
@State private var room: ConversationController?

// SDK-backed: own confirmed rows gain a context menu with Edit message /
// Delete message, the composer saves while editing, confirmDelete replaces the
// built-in dialog, and the trailing onController hands you the wrapper's
// controller once, before its first refresh, so a custom row can drive it.
try ConvoKitConversation(client: convoKit, conversationId: roomId, messageView: { context in
    AnyView(HStack {
        Text(context.message.text ?? "Attachment")
        if context.isEdited { Text("Edited").font(.caption2).accessibilityLabel("Edited") }
    }
    .contextMenu {
        if let edit = context.edit { Button("Edit message") { edit() } }
        if let remove = context.remove { Button("Delete message", role: .destructive) { Task { _ = await remove() } } }
    })
}, confirmDelete: { _ in await askTheUser() }, onController: { room = $0 })

// Controlled: edit mode is a pure function of editingMessage and the callbacks.
// Leave them out and no action renders.
ConversationView(
    conversation: state.conversation,
    messages: state.messages,
    currentUserId: state.currentUserId,
    readPositionByUserId: state.readPositionByUserId,
    onSendMessage: viewModel.send,
    editingMessage: viewModel.editingMessage,
    onEditMessage: { viewModel.startEditing($0.id) },
    onCancelEditing: { viewModel.cancelEditing() },
    onSaveEdit: { text in await viewModel.saveEdit(text) },
    onDeleteMessage: { message in await viewModel.deleteMessage(message.id) },
    confirmDelete: { _ in await askTheUser() }
)
```

### Quoted replies and jump to a message

-   `ConversationController` gains `replyTarget: Message?` (the row the next send quotes), `startReply(_ messageId:)` and `cancelReply()`.
-   Unlike editing, ANY member's row may be quoted: the rule is `canSend` (a live `READ_WRITE` session) plus a rendered, confirmed, non-tombstoned row, so an unknown, pending, removed or foreign-role case is a no-op.
-   Replying and editing are mutually exclusive in both directions.
-   The send stamps the reference on the optimistic row beside `revision: 0`, so the quoted block renders before acknowledgement, puts it on the wire through `SendMessageInput.replyToMessageId`, and clears `replyTarget` only when the send is confirmed — a failure keeps the quote exactly as it keeps the draft, and unlike edit mode the draft is never stashed.
-   A send that is not a reply omits the field entirely.
-   Quoted messages are resolved in batches: `replyPreviews: [String: ReplyPreviewState]` carries `.resolved(preview)`, the terminal `.unavailable` and — the distinct third state — no entry at all, which means "not yet resolved" and renders the reference with no quoted text, never the unavailable copy.
-   Rendering a page of replies costs one `getReplyPreviews` call, not one per row: a parent already in the loaded window is derived locally (truncated at 500 characters with `textTruncated` set) and costs no request, and a live-insert burst is debounced into a single batch whose handle is cleared by `stop()` and `retire()`.
-   An id requested in a call that RESOLVED and missing from its result becomes terminally `.unavailable` (the reference and the jump affordance stay); a call that REJECTS writes no entry at all — those ids stay unresolved, surface through `error` without evicting a row, and are re-requested on the next trigger — and a cached entry is invalidated by a deletion (terminal), by a row image, hydration or edit answer for the quoted row, and by a re-subscription.
-   `jumpToMessage(_ messageId:) -> Bool` highlights and scrolls to a row already in the window with no request; anything else replaces the window with one `getMessageContext` page centred on it and sets `windowMode` to `.jumped`, with `hasNewerMessages`, `isLoadingNewer`, `highlightedMessageId` (a flash of about two seconds) and `scrollTarget` (consumed once, through `scrollTargetHandled()`).
-   A jump is a WINDOW operation, never a re-open: the private state captured when the room opened, the acknowledged floor, the tombstones, edit mode and `replyTarget` all survive it, it arms no acknowledgement, it never calls the initial-load path, and it is a no-op while a send is in flight.
-   A coded `404 MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND` is not a failure but the guaranteed answer for a deleted quote: the preview becomes `.unavailable` and the window is untouched.
-   A jumped window withholds live inserts — ingestion runs to completion, but an insert is recorded rather than rendered and cannot be acknowledged while it is off screen, while edits, revisions and deletions for rows INSIDE the window still apply.
-   Both ends page through `getMessageContext`: `loadOlder()` follows the stored older cursor and the new `loadNewer()` the newer one, and a newer page that reaches the tail runs `returnToLatest()` rather than flipping the mode on the spot.
-   `returnToLatest() -> Bool` drops the window and reloads the newest page through the normal live loader, setting `windowMode = .live` BEFORE the request so inserts arriving during the round trip fold in under the usual precedence and the withheld rows are rendered — and acknowledged — at that moment; a failed reload restores the window and stays `.jumped`, and the highlight is carried through so the target re-anchors when it is still in the newest page.
-   `send` and `uploadAndSend` await it first, so a send is always confined to the live window while the quote survives the switch.
-   A queued refresh while jumped re-reads the jumped window with ONE bounded `getMessageContext` anchored on the jump target (or, once the window has been paged, on its midpoint), sized to the window and capped at 100, tombstones only inside the returned range, and leaves the owed tail reconcile owed so it flushes on the return to `.live`; `getConversation` still runs exactly as in live mode.
-   `ConversationView` gains trailing defaulted `replyTarget:`, `onReplyToMessage:`, `onCancelReply:`, `replyPreviewByMessageId:`, `onJumpToMessage:`, `highlightedMessageId:`, `scrollTarget:`, `onScrollTargetHandled:`, `hasNewerMessages:`, `isLoadingNewer:`, `onLoadNewer:` and `onReturnToLatest:`; without the callbacks every row and the composer render exactly as in the previous release.
-   `MessageContext` gains additive `canReply`, `reply`, `replyPreview` and `jumpToReplyTarget` — the last two are non-nil only when the row is a reply, and `canReply` drops the own-row term (`onReplyToMessage != nil && confirmed && canSend && role != "READ"`) and is never routed through an edit or delete override.
-   Default rows: a reply shows a quoted block above its content with three branches — the quoted author and their text, the terminal `Original message unavailable`, and, while unresolved, `Quoted message` — activatable to jump when `onJumpToMessage` is wired (accessible names `Quoted message from` the author, `Original message unavailable`, `Quoted message`).
-   An eligible row gains `Reply` in the context menu and as a named accessibility action, after the `Edit message` / `Delete message` pair.
-   The composer shows a `Replying to` strip with the quoted line and `Cancel` (accessible name `Cancel reply`, Escape) while `replyTarget` is set; edit mode wins if a host sets both.
-   A jumped window shows `Load newer messages` and `Jump to latest` at the newer edge, and nothing at all while `live`.
-   `ConvoKitTheme.highlight` is an additive token for the jump flash, following `accent` at low opacity until set (the `badge` pattern), and `ConvoKitConversation` wires every new prop from its controller.
-   There is still no public adapter protocol.
-   Both new routes need the paired 0.9 backend: against an older one they answer an uncoded 404, which is never "the message is gone" — the batch stays unresolved (rows keep their reference with no quoted text), a jump leaves the window untouched, the failure surfaces once, and `supportsReplyPreviews` / `supportsJump` turn false for the life of the store so the affordances disappear instead of failing repeatedly.
-   A coded `MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND` never trips them.
-   Sending a quote to an older backend degrades visibly and is not detected: the backend parses only `text` and `media`, so it drops the unknown `replyToMessageId` and stores the message with no reference — the optimistic row shows the quote and the confirmed row replaces it without one.
-   The message is delivered; only the reference is lost.

```swift
// SDK-backed: confirmed rows gain Reply in the context menu, quoted blocks
// resolve themselves in one batched request per page, and tapping one jumps.
try ConvoKitConversation(client: convoKit, conversationId: roomId, messageView: { context in
    AnyView(VStack(alignment: .leading) {
        // Three states, and the third is not the second: resolved, gone, and not
        // resolved yet (the reference with no quoted text).
        if context.message.replyToMessageId != nil {
            Button {
                context.jumpToReplyTarget?()
            } label: {
                switch context.replyPreview {
                case .resolved(let preview): Text(preview.text ?? "Attachment")
                case .unavailable: Text("Original message unavailable")
                case nil: Text("Quoted message")
                }
            }
            .disabled(context.jumpToReplyTarget == nil)
        }
        Text(context.message.text ?? "Attachment")
    }
    .contextMenu {
        if let reply = context.reply { Button("Reply") { reply() } }
    })
}, onController: { room = $0 })

// Controlled: reply and jump state stays store-owned. Leave the callbacks out
// and every row and the composer render exactly as before.
ConversationView(
    conversation: state.conversation,
    messages: state.messages,
    currentUserId: state.currentUserId,
    readPositionByUserId: state.readPositionByUserId,
    onSendMessage: viewModel.send,
    replyTarget: viewModel.replyTarget,
    onReplyToMessage: { viewModel.startReply($0.id) },
    onCancelReply: { viewModel.cancelReply() },
    replyPreviewByMessageId: viewModel.replyPreviews,
    onJumpToMessage: { messageId in Task { _ = await viewModel.jumpToMessage(messageId) } },
    highlightedMessageId: viewModel.highlightedMessageId,
    scrollTarget: viewModel.scrollTarget,
    onScrollTargetHandled: { viewModel.scrollTargetHandled() },
    hasNewerMessages: viewModel.hasNewerMessages,
    isLoadingNewer: viewModel.isLoadingNewer,
    onLoadNewer: { await viewModel.loadNewer() },
    onReturnToLatest: { _ = await viewModel.returnToLatest() }
)
```

### Read receipts

-   Reads are positions.
-   `ConversationController.readPositionByUserId` is seeded from each participant's `readPosition`, advanced from realtime read events, and paired with `readAtByUserId` (acknowledgement times) as the fallback for members without a position; `ConversationView` accepts both.
-   SDK-backed views acknowledge the newest rendered message, only while the scene is active; a read held back while inactive is sent when the scene becomes active again, and every acknowledgement carries the `privateStateVersion` captured when the room opened so reading clears the user's own unread marker only while it is still current.
-   Both `markReadOnLoad` and `markReadOnReceive` false means no read request is ever sent.
-   By default, a confirmed message without readers shows only its timestamp, and read state shows Read or Read by N next to a checkmark; ConvoKit does not currently report recipient delivery.

```swift
// A member's read position decides by conversation order; lastReadAt is the
// fallback for members without one. The SDK-backed controller does this for you.
let readers = state.conversation.participants.filter { participant in
    participant.appUserId != message.senderId &&
    readThrough(
        position: state.readPositionByUserId[participant.appUserId]
            ?? participant.readPosition,
        lastReadAt: state.readAtByUserId[participant.appUserId]
            ?? participant.lastReadAt,
        message: message
    )
}

// ConvoKitConversation gates reads on scenePhase == .active. When you drive
// ConversationController behind a controlled view, report visibility yourself.
controller.setVisible(scenePhase == .active)
```

### Stable local timestamps

Pending outgoing messages show `Sending…` without a provisional timestamp or receipt. After acknowledgement, SwiftUI renders the server timestamp in the viewer's current timezone. Custom views can check `Message.isConvoKitPending`.

### Session lifecycle

Connect the user before creating subscriptions or SDK-backed UI. Your token provider must fetch fresh tokens from your authenticated backend.

On sign-out or account change, dispose the current UI controllers and subscriptions, then disconnect the client. Create a new adapter or controller after the next successful login, even when signing back in as the same user.

See [authentication](https://convokit.app/docs/auth) for the token flow and [messaging behavior](https://convokit.app/docs/messaging) for read receipts, retries, timestamps, and what the SDK-backed UI handles automatically.

Android UI

# Ship native Compose chat quickly, then replace exactly the pieces your product owns.

The Android UI package adds SDK-backed and controlled conversation components, inbox previews and unread counts, pagination, realtime state, media, read receipts, Material 3 theming, and replaceable Compose slots on top of the native Kotlin SDK.

Published`app.convokit:convokit-android-ui 0.10.1``app.convokit:convokit-android 0.10.0`

### Composable defaults with native Android ownership

-   Start with controller-backed components or connect presentation-only views to your ViewModel.
-   Both layers render the same default components and customization slots.
-   Version 0.10.1 anchors compact reaction chips and a quick picker to each message, with a full picker for custom emoji.

[Maven artifact](https://maven.convokit.app/app/convokit/convokit-android-ui/0.10.1/convokit-android-ui-0.10.1.pom) [Public examples](https://github.com/ConvoKitApp/ConvoKit-Android-UI-Examples)

### Install from the public Maven feed

No registry login or GitHub token is required. API 23+, Kotlin 2.1, and Java 17 are supported.

```kotlin
dependencyResolutionManagement {
    repositories {
        google()
        mavenCentral()
        maven("https://maven.convokit.app/")
    }
}

dependencies {
    implementation("app.convokit:convokit-android:0.10.0")
    implementation("app.convokit:convokit-android-ui:0.10.1")
}
```

### Choose the ownership layer

-   Use SDK-backed components for speed or controlled views when your app owns state, caching, analytics, or authorization.
-   A custom `ConvoKitUiClient` implementation must implement the abstract `markConversationRead(conversationId, throughMessageId: String?, privateStateVersion: Int?)`, forward the target and the version unchanged, and reject an unknown target with a `ConvoKitException` whose code is `MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND` so the controller can acknowledge the next newest message; the one- and two-argument members delegate to it with a null version.
-   Do not override the three-argument member with a body that delegates to a two-argument implementation: that drops the version, so acknowledgements never clear the marker.
-   It must also implement the abstract `suspend fun listInbox(limit: Int, cursor: String?, archived: Boolean): InboxPage`, `markConversationUnread(conversationId): ConversationPrivateState` and `clearConversationUnread(conversationId, ifVersion: Int? = null): ClearUnreadResult` (answering a no-op clear with `cleared` false rather than an exception);`val inboxActivity: Flow<Unit>` defaults to an empty flow, so override it to receive activity signals.
-   The three-argument read and the two marker members are a breaking change for custom implementers, like `listInbox` was in the previous release.
-   `DefaultConvoKitUiClient` forwards all of them to the core SDK.
-   A custom `pageLoader` keeps the creation-order list with empty `summaries`.
-   Since this release the interface also has the abstract `editMessage(messageId, text: String?, revision: Int): Message` and `deleteMessage(messageId)`: forward `text` unchanged (null clears a caption and must reach the wire as JSON `null`, never omitted), send `revision` as the expected revision, surface backend answers as `ConvoKitException` (409 with code `REVISION_CONFLICT`, 404 with code `MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND`; a 404 without that code is an error that keeps the row), and never change attachments from `editMessage`.
-   Both are abstract and therefore a breaking change for custom implementers, like `listInbox` was in an earlier release; `DefaultConvoKitUiClient` wires them through the core's author calls.

`ConvoKitConversationList``ConvoKitConversation`Loading, pagination, previews, unread counts and the private unread marker, realtime, sending, editing and deleting your own messages, typing, and read state included.

`ConvoKitConversationListView``ConvoKitConversationView`Application-controlled state and callbacks with the same presentation layer.

### Connect the core SDK

Adapt one connected client for all SDK-backed UI. It uses https://api.convokit.app automatically.

```kotlin
val sdk = ConvoKitClient(
    clientId = "your-public-client-id",
    tokenProvider = TokenProvider { appUserId ->
        yourApi.issueConvoKitToken(appUserId).token
    },
)

sdk.connectUser(currentUser.id)
val uiClient = DefaultConvoKitUiClient(sdk)
```

### Render list and room

Select a conversation ID and hand it to the realtime component.

```kotlin
var roomId by remember { mutableStateOf<String?>(null) }

ConvoKitConversationList(
    client = uiClient,
    onConversationSelected = { roomId = it.id },
    initialFilter = ConversationFilter(query = search),
)

roomId?.let { id ->
    ConvoKitConversation(
        client = uiClient,
        conversationId = id,
        onAddAttachment = ::openAttachmentPicker,
        onAttachmentClick = { _, media -> openMedia(media) },
    )
}
```

### Control behavior, layout, and each visual seam

Keep the default surface, replace one focused block, or supply a complete row while retaining the package controllers.

### Conversation list behavior

### Conversation list UI

### Conversation behavior

`conversationId / client / onController``messagePageSize / reverseMessages``markReadOnLoad / markReadOnReceive / setVisible``startEditing / saveEdit / cancelEditing / deleteMessage``startReplying / cancelReplying / jumpToMessage / loadNewerMessages / returnToLatest / clearHighlight``typingTimeout / onBack / attachment callbacks`

### Conversation UI

### Controlled state

### Theme tokens

`light and dark color palettes``incoming / outgoing / receipt / badge colors``highlight color (accent at low opacity)``corner radii / avatar size``content padding / spacing / message width`

### Controlled components and content slots

The host owns state and replaces only product-specific pieces.

```kotlin
ConvoKitConversationView(
    conversation = state.conversation,
    messages = state.messages,
    currentUserId = state.currentUserId,
    readPositionByUserId = state.readPositionByUserId,
    readAtByUserId = state.readAtByUserId,
    typingUserIds = state.typingUserIds,
    isSending = state.isSending,
    hasOlderMessages = state.hasOlder,
    onLoadOlder = viewModel::loadOlder,
    onSendMessage = viewModel::send,
    headerContent = { conversation, _, refresh ->
        ProductHeader(conversation, refresh)
    },
    mediaContent = { media, message, _, defaultContent ->
        if (media is LocationMedia) MapPreview(media)
        else defaultContent()
    },
    readReceiptContent = { _, readers ->
        ReaderAvatars(readers)
    },
)
```

### Inbox previews and unread counts

-   The SDK-backed `ConvoKitConversationList` shows each room's latest message, its activity time in the device timezone, and an unread badge.
-   The preview reads `You: …` for your own latest message, `Name: …` for a named sender in a room with more than two participants, and the body alone otherwise; a media-only message reads `Photo`, the file name or `File`, `Location`, or `Contact`.
-   The badge renders while `unreadCount` is above 0 or the count is capped, shows the count up to 99 and `99+` above that or whenever the count is capped, and carries the accessible name `N unread` (`99+ unread` when capped) with the visible label hidden from the accessibility tree; the title is bold while unread.
-   A room marked unread with a count of 0 renders a numberless dot instead (see Mark unread).
-   Its color is the `ConvoKitUiColors.badge` token (defaulted to the accent; the label uses `onPrimary`).
-   `ConversationListState` carries `summaries` (a map from conversation ID to `InboxSummary`) and `currentUserId`.
-   The `inboxItem` slot, `(conversation, summary: InboxSummary?, chronologicalIndex, onClick)`, replaces the row with access to the summary and wins over the unchanged `conversationItem` slot; `DefaultConversationItem(conversation, onClick, summary = …, currentUserId = …)` renders the default row, and the controlled `ConvoKitConversationListView` accepts `summaries` and `currentUserId` (absent means the previous rows and no `You:` prefix).
-   Rows arrive in inbox order and pages are merged by conversation ID with the later entry winning, re-sorted by activity, then ID; `ConversationFilter.matches(conversation)` is the predicate half for hosts that order rows themselves.
-   Activity signals are coalesced into one refresh per `activityRefreshWindowMs` (default 500; 0 refreshes on every signal), while membership and metadata changes refresh immediately.
-   If the inbox route answers 404, the list falls back to conversation paging without previews for the rest of the controller's life.

```kotlin
ConvoKitConversationList(
    client = uiClient,
    onConversationSelected = { roomId = it.id },
    activityRefreshWindowMs = 500, // default; 0 refreshes on every activity signal
    inboxItem = { conversation, summary, _, onClick ->
        val badge = summary?.takeIf { it.unreadCount > 0 || it.unreadCountCapped }?.let {
            if (it.unreadCount <= 99 && !it.unreadCountCapped) it.unreadCount.toString() else "99+"
        }
        SupportRow(conversation, preview = summary?.latestMessage?.text, onClick = onClick) {
            when {
                badge != null -> Text(badge)
                // Marked unread with nothing new: a dot, never an invented count.
                summary?.isUnread == true -> Box(
                    Modifier.size(8.dp).clip(CircleShape).background(colors.badge)
                        .semantics { contentDescription = "Unread" },
                )
            }
        }
    },
)

// Controlled hosts pass the same data explicitly.
ConvoKitConversationListView(
    conversations = state.conversations,
    summaries = state.summaries,
    currentUserId = state.currentUserId,
    onConversationSelected = ::open,
)
```

### Mark unread

-   `ConvoKitConversationListController` exposes `markUnread(conversationId)` and `clearUnread(conversationId, ifVersion: Int? = null): Boolean`; `ConvoKitConversationList` hands you its controller through `onController`.
-   The marker is private to the connected user: other members, webhooks and read events never see it, and `unreadCount` is untouched.
-   `clearUnread` returns the server's `cleared` (this request removed a marker), not whether the room is read; an unmarked room or a stale `ifVersion` returns false without an error.
-   After either response the row's current summary takes `unreadMarkedAt` and `privateStateVersion` as one unit and `isUnread` is recomputed, only while the response is not older than the stored version, so a delayed response never brings back a marker a newer action removed; failures set `error` without evicting rows.
-   Every `InboxSummary` carries `isUnread`, `unreadMarkedAt` and `privateStateVersion` (trailing, defaulted, so existing literals keep compiling).
-   A row is unread (bold title) when `isUnread`, the count is above 0, or the count is capped; a count or a capped count keeps the numeric badge, and a room unread only through the marker renders a numberless 8 dp dot in the `badge` color whose accessible name is `Unread`, never an invented count.
-   There is no built-in row affordance: wire a menu or swipe through `inboxItem` and `onController`.
-   SDK-backed rooms capture the user's own `membership.privateStateVersion` once, the first time the room opens (also after a transient first-load failure), never from a later reconcile, and send it with every acknowledgement of that open, so reading clears the marker only while the version is still current and a mark made after the open survives until the room is reopened.
-   A room opened with the marker and nothing rendered calls the adapter's `clearConversationUnread` with the captured version once per open, under the same conditions and visibility gating as the load acknowledgement; `cleared` false is not an error.
-   Marker changes on other devices arrive through the throttled activity refresh.
-   Lists built with the previous release ignore `isUnread` and keep their counts.

```kotlin
var list by remember { mutableStateOf<ConvoKitConversationListController?>(null) }

// No built-in row affordance: wire a menu or swipe through inboxItem and onController.
ConvoKitConversationList(
    client = uiClient,
    onConversationSelected = { roomId = it.id },
    onController = { list = it },
    inboxItem = { conversation, summary, _, onClick ->
        SupportRow(
            conversation,
            unread = summary?.isUnread == true,
            onClick = onClick,
            onMarkUnread = { scope.launch { list?.markUnread(conversation.id) } },
        )
    },
)

// Remove the marker without opening the room, only while it still has the
// version the row shows. Returns the server's cleared: false is not an error.
val cleared = list?.clearUnread(conversation.id, ifVersion = summary.privateStateVersion)

// SDK-backed rooms capture membership.privateStateVersion when they open and
// send it with every acknowledgement of that open; nothing to wire.
ConvoKitConversation(client = uiClient, conversationId = roomId)
```

### Edit and delete your own messages

-   `ConvoKitConversationController` owns edit mode: `ConversationState` carries `editingMessage` (the message being edited, as the user saw it when editing began; null outside edit mode) and `canEditMessages` / `canDeleteMessages` (a bound session whose known role is not `READ`), all trailing defaulted fields so positional `ConversationState(...)` calls keep compiling; the controller exposes `startEditing(messageId)`, `cancelEditing()`, `saveEdit(text): Boolean` and `deleteMessage(messageId): Boolean`, and `ConvoKitConversation` hands you its controller through `onController`.
-   `startEditing` is a no-op for another member's row, a pending row, a removed row, a read-only role and after `close()`; it sends nothing, not even a typing update.
-   `saveEdit` trims the text and sends the revision captured when editing began, never the live row's, so the server compares against what the user saw.
-   A stale revision (409 `REVISION_CONFLICT`) reloads the row once through `getMessage`: the row shows the current content, the snapshot moves to it so the banner shows what changed and the next save carries the fresh revision, `error` carries the conflict (a `ConvoKitException` with code `REVISION_CONFLICT`) and the edited text stays in the field.
-   The same state is entered without a request when a newer revision of the edited row arrives while editing.
-   A 404 with code `MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND` on the save or the reload removes the row and ends edit mode; any other failure (403, network, a server error, or an uncoded 404 from an older backend) keeps the row, the draft and edit mode and only sets `error`.
-   `deleteMessage` is never optimistic: the row goes once the adapter answers or reports `MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND`, and stays on any other failure; late responses and updates for a removed row are dropped, and a removal by any path ends edit mode on it.
-   When rows for one message meet, the higher `revision` wins and a lower one never overwrites; equal revisions keep the timestamp rule.
-   Default rows: with `onEditMessage` / `onDeleteMessage` bound (the SDK-backed view binds them while `canEditMessages` / `canDeleteMessages` hold), the current user's confirmed rows offer a long press (accessible action `Message actions`) opening `Edit message` / `Delete message`; deleting asks `Delete this message?` with `Delete` (named `Confirm delete`) and `Cancel` (named `Cancel delete`), or `confirmDelete: (suspend (Message) -> Boolean)?` instead.
-   Edited rows (`Message.isEdited`) show `Edited` beside the time with the content description `Edited`, for own and foreign rows alike; foreign rows, pending rows, rows under a `READ` role and views without the callbacks render exactly as before.
-   Default composer: while `editingMessage` is set a banner (`Editing message`, the original text, `Cancel` named `Cancel editing`, announced as a polite live region) sits above the composer, the field is prefilled silently with the unsent draft stashed, and the one submit handed to the default and custom composers calls `onSaveEdit` with the trimmed text instead of sending, so custom composers need no branching and see `isSending` true while a save runs.
-   The default button reads `Save` (named `Save message`) instead of `Send` and is enabled while the trimmed field is non-empty or the edited row has attachments, so saving an empty field on a message with attachments sends a null text and clears the caption while every attachment stays; a text-only message can never be saved empty.
-   The field is not cleared during the request; success and Cancel restore the stash and report `onTypingChanged` from it; an external clear keeps user-changed text and restores the stash only when the field is empty or still equals the message text.
-   Controlled views: `ConvoKitConversationView` gains the trailing `editingMessage: Message? = null`, `onEditMessage: ((Message) -> Unit)?`, `onSaveEdit: ((Message, String, (Boolean) -> Unit) -> Unit)?` (completion style like `onSendMessageResult`; false keeps the text and edit mode), `onCancelEdit: (() -> Unit)?`, `onDeleteMessage: ((Message, (Boolean) -> Unit) -> Unit)?` and `confirmDelete`; `ConvoKitMessageListView` gains `onEditMessage`, `onDeleteMessage` and `confirmDelete`.
-   With none of them bound the surface is the previous release's.
-   `ComposerContent`, `MessageItemContent` and every other slot keep their arity: a custom row reads `Message.isEdited` and reaches edit mode through the controller, a custom composer reads `editingMessage` from the state.
-   `DefaultComposer` gains `editing` and `allowEmpty`; `DefaultMessageItem` gains `onEditMessage`, `onDeleteMessage` and `confirmDelete`.
-   Deleting a message removes it and its attachments from the conversation for every member and cannot be undone; files already received or downloaded cannot be retracted.
-   The core's `Message` data class gained a trailing `revision` field, so consumers rebuild against the paired release.
-   Clients built with the previous release ignore `revision` and show no actions; against an older backend the author routes answer an uncoded 404 that only surfaces as `error`, and every row reads as revision 0.

```kotlin
// SDK-backed: own confirmed rows offer Message actions on a long press, the
// composer saves while editing, and confirmDelete replaces the built-in dialog.
ConvoKitConversation(
    client = uiClient,
    conversationId = roomId,
    confirmDelete = { message -> askTheUser("Delete this message?") },
)

// Controlled: edit mode is a pure function of editingMessage and the callbacks.
// Leave them out and no action renders.
val controller = remember { ConvoKitConversationController(roomId, uiClient, scope) }
val state by controller.state.collectAsState()

ConvoKitConversationView(
    conversation = state.conversation!!,
    messages = state.messages,
    currentUserId = state.currentUserId,
    onSendMessage = { text -> scope.launch { controller.sendMessage(text) } },
    readPositionByUserId = state.readPositionByUserId,
    editingMessage = state.editingMessage,
    onEditMessage = { controller.startEditing(it.id) },
    onSaveEdit = { _, text, complete -> scope.launch { complete(controller.saveEdit(text)) } },
    onCancelEdit = controller::cancelEditing,
    onDeleteMessage = { message, complete -> scope.launch { complete(controller.deleteMessage(message.id)) } },
    // The slot signatures are unchanged: a custom row reads Message.isEdited and
    // reaches edit mode through the controller; a custom composer's send saves
    // while editing.
    messageItem = { message, _, mine, sender, readers ->
        MyMessageBubble(
            message = message,
            edited = message.isEdited,
            onEdit = if (mine) ({ controller.startEditing(message.id) }) else null,
            onDelete = if (mine) ({ scope.launch { controller.deleteMessage(message.id) } }) else null,
        )
    },
    composerContent = { text, onTextChange, sending, send, attachment ->
        MyComposer(
            text = text,
            onTextChange = onTextChange,
            editing = state.editingMessage,
            onCancelEdit = controller::cancelEditing,
            onSend = send,
        )
    },
)
```

### Quoted replies and jump to a message

-   `ConvoKitConversationController` owns the composer's reply target and the history window.
-   `startReplying(messageId)` captures any rendered, confirmed row (own or foreign — any member may quote any row) into `ConversationState.replyTarget`, `cancelReplying()` drops it, and the next `sendMessage` stamps its id on the optimistic row, sends it as `replyToMessageId` and clears the target on success; a failed send keeps the quote.
-   Replying and editing are mutually exclusive, deleting the quoted row clears a pending target, and `ConversationState.canReplyToMessages` is true for a bound session whose known role is not `READ`.
-   `ConversationState` also gains `replyPreviews`, `highlightedMessageId`, `scrollTarget`, `suppressPagination`, `hasNewerMessages`, `isLoadingNewer`, `windowMode` and `canJumpToMessages`; all ten are trailing defaulted fields, so positional `ConversationState(...)` calls keep compiling.
-   The controller adds `jumpToMessage(id)`, `returnToLatest()`, `loadNewerMessages()` and `clearHighlight()`.
-   Quoted text is resolved in batches, never per row: `replyPreviews` maps `replyToMessageId` to `ConvoKitReplyPreview.Resolved(ReplyPreview)` or the terminal `ConvoKitReplyPreview.Unavailable`, and a missing key is the distinct third state, "not yet resolved" — render the reference with no quoted text, never the unavailable copy.
-   One `getReplyPreviews` call runs after every page load, reconcile and debounced live-insert burst, covering only the references that are not derivable from the loaded window, not already terminal and either uncached or stale; a parent inside the window is derived locally (500-character excerpt with `textTruncated`) and costs no request, and entries no rendered row references are dropped.
-   Invalidation is explicit, because row precedence cannot see a parent's revision bump from a reply row: a deletion is terminal, an edit of a parent refreshes it in-window and marks it stale out-of-window, and a rejoin marks every non-terminal entry stale.
-   A call that resolves without an id caches `Unavailable` for it; a call that rejects writes no entry at all, leaves those references unresolved for the next batch and surfaces through `error` without evicting rows.
-   `jumpToMessage(id)` highlights and scrolls a target already rendered, and otherwise replaces the window with one bounded context page centred on it (`windowMode` becomes `ConvoKitWindowMode.JUMPED`).
-   A jump is a window operation, never a re-open: the captured `privateStateVersion`, the acknowledgement floor, the tombstones and edit mode all survive, no room DTO is re-fetched and no `markReadOnLoad` acknowledgement is armed.
-   While jumped, realtime inserts are recorded but not rendered (hydration, send confirmation and tombstone bookkeeping keep running, and edits of rows inside the window still apply), the deferred rows are drained with the read acknowledgements they owed the moment the window is live again, no targeted acknowledgement is sent or armed, and every queued reconcile becomes one bounded re-read of the same window that tombstones only inside the returned range while the tail-anchored reconcile stays owed and runs on the return to live.
-   Sending from a jumped window returns to the live tail first, and a jump is refused while a send is in flight.
-   `ConvoKitWindowMode.LIVE` / `.JUMPED` and `ConvoKitReplyPreview` are new public types.
-   Default rows: with `onReplyToMessage` bound, every confirmed row under a non-`READ` role offers `Reply` in the existing long-press menu (`Message actions`), above `Edit message` / `Delete message`.
-   A row whose `Message.replyToMessageId` is set renders a quoted block (`Quoted message`) above its text with three branches and no fourth: the quoted author and excerpt, `Original message unavailable` for a terminal preview, and the bare reference while it is unresolved; with `onJumpToMessage` bound the block activates it (`Go to quoted message`).
-   The highlighted row tints with the new `ConvoKitUiColors.highlight` token (accent at low opacity), fades over about two seconds and is announced politely.
-   Rows without the new callbacks, and rows that are not replies, render byte-identically to the previous release.
-   Composer: while `replyTarget` is set a banner (`Replying to` the author, the quoted text, a `Cancel` named `Cancel reply`) sits where the editing banner does; editing wins when both are somehow set, and unlike edit mode the reply strip never touches the draft.
-   `ComposerContent` keeps its arity, so custom composers reach `replyTarget` through `ConversationState` (`onController`).
-   New row slot: `ConvoKitMessageItemScope` carries the five arguments of the frozen `MessageItemContent` (`message`, `chronologicalIndex`, `isCurrentUser`, `sender`, `readerIds`) plus `replyPreview`, `isReply`, `canReply`, `reply()`, `jumpToReplyTarget()` and `isHighlighted`, and reaches rows through the new trailing `messageItemScope` parameter beside `messageItem`; when both are supplied the scope slot wins, and `MessageItemContent` and every other typealias keep their signatures for ever.
-   Controlled views: `ConvoKitConversationView` gains `messageItemScope`, `replyTarget`, `onReplyToMessage`, `onCancelReply`, `replyPreviewByMessageId`, `onJumpToMessage`, `highlightedMessageId`, `hasNewerMessages`, `isLoadingNewer`, `onLoadNewer`, `onReturnToLatest`, `scrollTarget`, `suppressPagination` and `onScrollTargetHandled`; `ConvoKitMessageListView` gains all of them except `replyTarget`, `onCancelReply` and `onReturnToLatest`; `ConvoKitConversation` gains `messageItemScope`, `scrollTarget`, `suppressPagination` and `onScrollTargetHandled`.
-   All are trailing defaults, and the list gains a newer-edge pagination trigger beside the older-edge one, active only while `onLoadNewer` is bound, with both edges carrying the `suppressPagination` guard so a jump's own scroll never loads a page.
-   Breaking for custom `ConvoKitUiClient` implementations, like `markConversationUnread` and `editMessage` / `deleteMessage` before it: `sendMessage` gains a trailing `replyToMessageId: String? = null` parameter — added to the member rather than introduced as a second overload, so an adapter that silently dropped the reply target cannot compile — and two required abstract members arrive, `getReplyPreviews(conversationId, messageIds)` and `getMessageContext(conversationId, messageId, olderCursor, newerCursor, limit)`.
-   There is no interface default for either, so a test adapter cannot skip the seam; `DefaultConvoKitUiClient` implements all three.
-   Against an older backend both new routes answer an uncoded 404 (`HTTP_ERROR`), which is never read as "the message is gone": preview references stay unresolved rather than becoming `Unavailable`, a jump leaves the window untouched, the failure surfaces once through `error`, and after the first uncoded 404 `canJumpToMessages` goes false for the life of the store so the affordance disappears.
-   A coded `404 MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND` never trips that: it is a real missing target and is recorded as the terminal `Unavailable` preview with no error at all.
-   Sending a quote to an older backend degrades visibly and is not detected: the backend parses only `text` and `media`, so it drops the unknown `replyToMessageId` and stores the message with no reference — the optimistic row shows the quote and the confirmed row replaces it without one.
-   The message is delivered; only the reference is lost.

```kotlin
// SDK-backed: confirmed rows offer Reply in the long-press menu, quoted blocks
// resolve themselves in one batched request per page, and tapping one jumps.
ConvoKitConversation(client = uiClient, conversationId = roomId)

// Controlled: reply and jump state stays controller-owned. Leave the callbacks
// out and nothing renders.
val controller = remember { ConvoKitConversationController(roomId, uiClient, scope) }
val state by controller.state.collectAsState()

ConvoKitConversationView(
    conversation = state.conversation!!,
    messages = state.messages,
    currentUserId = state.currentUserId,
    onSendMessage = { text -> scope.launch { controller.sendMessage(text) } },
    replyTarget = state.replyTarget,
    onReplyToMessage = { controller.startReplying(it.id) },
    onCancelReply = controller::cancelReplying,
    replyPreviewByMessageId = state.replyPreviews,
    onJumpToMessage = { messageId -> scope.launch { controller.jumpToMessage(messageId) } },
    highlightedMessageId = state.highlightedMessageId,
    scrollTarget = state.scrollTarget,
    suppressPagination = state.suppressPagination,
    onScrollTargetHandled = controller::clearHighlight,
    hasNewerMessages = state.hasNewerMessages,
    isLoadingNewer = state.isLoadingNewer,
    onLoadNewer = { scope.launch { controller.loadNewerMessages() } },
    onReturnToLatest = { scope.launch { controller.returnToLatest() } },
    // The new scope slot carries the five frozen messageItem arguments plus the
    // reply members, and wins when both are supplied.
    messageItemScope = { scope ->
        MyMessageBubble(
            message = scope.message,
            // Three states, and the third is not the second: resolved, gone, and
            // not resolved yet (the reference with no quoted text).
            quote = when (val preview = scope.replyPreview) {
                is ConvoKitReplyPreview.Resolved -> preview.preview.text
                ConvoKitReplyPreview.Unavailable -> "Original message unavailable"
                null -> if (scope.isReply) "Quoted message" else null
            },
            onQuoteClick = scope.jumpToReplyTarget,
            onReply = scope.reply,
            highlighted = scope.isHighlighted,
        )
    },
    composerContent = { text, onTextChange, sending, send, attachment ->
        MyComposer(
            text = text,
            onTextChange = onTextChange,
            replying = state.replyTarget,
            onCancelReply = controller::cancelReplying,
            onSend = send,
        )
    },
)
```

### Filtering and pagination

Combine server archive paging with local text, participant, predicate, and ordering rules. SDK-backed lists arrive in inbox order (latest surviving message, then creation time); setting `comparator` replaces that order for the whole list.

```kotlin
val controller = ConvoKitConversationListController(
    client = uiClient,
    scope = viewModelScope,
    pageSize = 25,
    initialFilter = ConversationFilter(archived = false),
)

controller.setFilter(
    ConversationFilter(
        query = "design",
        participantIds = setOf("app-user-42"),
        predicate = { it.description != null },
        comparator = compareBy { it.displayTitle },
    ),
)
```

### Read receipts

-   Reads are positions.
-   The controller seeds `readPositionByUserId` from each participant's `readPosition`, advances it from realtime read events, and keeps `readAtByUserId` (acknowledgement times) as the fallback for participants without a position.
-   SDK-backed components acknowledge the newest rendered message, only while the host lifecycle is started; a read held back while stopped is sent when the screen starts again, and every acknowledgement carries the `privateStateVersion` captured when the room opened so reading clears the user's own unread marker only while it is still current.
-   With both `markReadOnLoad` and `markReadOnReceive` false, the controller never sends a read on its own; only an explicit `markRead()` call does.
-   By default, a confirmed message without readers is marked Sent (single check) and read state shows Read by N (double check); ConvoKit does not currently report recipient delivery.

```kotlin
val state by controller.state.collectAsState()

// ConvoKitConversation follows the host lifecycle for you. When you own the
// controller, report visibility so reads wait until the screen is started.
controller.setVisible(isScreenStarted)

// Newest read position per participant, by conversation order, plus
// acknowledgement times as the fallback for participants without one.
val readersForMessage = state.readerIdsFor(message)

ConvoKitMessageListView(
    conversation = conversation,
    messages = state.messages,
    currentUserId = state.currentUserId,
    readPositionByUserId = state.readPositionByUserId,
    readAtByUserId = state.readAtByUserId,
    readReceiptContent = { _, readerIds ->
        Text("Seen by ${readerIds.size}")
    },
)
```

### Stable local timestamps

Pending outgoing messages show `Sending…` without a provisional timestamp or receipt. After acknowledgement, the server timestamp is formatted in the current Android system timezone. Custom content can check `Message.isConvoKitPending`.

### Images and files

Upload with the core SDK, then render structured media with authenticated protected downloads.

```kotlin
val url = sdk.uploadMessageMedia(
    conversationId = roomId,
    input = UploadInput(
        bytes = selectedBytes,
        fileName = "screenshot.png",
        contentType = "image/png",
    ),
)

controller.sendMessage(
    text = "Attached for review",
    media = listOf(ImageMedia(url = url, name = "screenshot.png")),
)
```

### Joining a room by ID

Your backend grants membership; the UI receives the authorized conversation ID.

```kotlin
suspend fun joinAndOpenRoom(roomId: String) {
    // Your backend authenticates the app user and grants membership.
    appBackend.joinConvoKitRoom(roomId)

    // The UI loads only after the user is authorized for this ID.
    selectedConversationId = roomId
}
```

Security boundary

### The client secret never belongs in Android.

Android receives the public client ID and a short-lived user token. Your backend keeps the client secret, authenticates the host user, and enforces any room-joining policy.

### Session lifecycle

Connect the user before creating subscriptions or SDK-backed UI. Your token provider must fetch fresh tokens from your authenticated backend.

On sign-out or account change, dispose the current UI controllers and subscriptions, then disconnect the client. Create a new adapter or controller after the next successful login, even when signing back in as the same user.

See [authentication](https://convokit.app/docs/auth) for the token flow and [messaging behavior](https://convokit.app/docs/messaging) for read receipts, retries, timestamps, and what the SDK-backed UI handles automatically.
